questions.question: Evaluate: 16 + 18 ÷ 6 - 3 × 3
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply BODMAS: solve division and multiplication first

18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 3 × 3 = 9

Expression becomes: 16 + 3 − 9

16 + 3 = 19, then 19 − 9 = 10

**∴ Answer = 10**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

16 + 18 ÷ 6 − 3 × 3

**Concept Used:**

BODMAS rule

**Calculation:**

16 + 18 ÷ 6 - 3 × 3

⇒ 16 + 3 − 3 × 3

⇒ 16 + 3 − 9

⇒ 19 − 9

⇒ 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Order: Brackets → Orders → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction

Left to Right Rule

Division and multiplication are solved from left to right when both appear

Sign Simplification

After higher operations, solve addition and subtraction sequentially

Common Error

Avoid solving left to right blindly without following BODMAS

questions.question: In Windows 11, which built-in tool opens immediately when a user presses the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + Esc?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Task Manager**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Task Manager** is a system monitor and startup manager utility included with **Microsoft Windows** systems that allows users to view and manage active processes.
 
• In **Windows 11**, pressing the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** opens the **Task Manager** immediately without requiring any further clicks or navigating through the security screen. ***Hence, the statement regarding Task Manager being the direct result of this shortcut is correct.***
 
• The **Task Manager** provides real-time data on the utilization of system resources such as the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **Random Access Memory (RAM)**, **Disk**, **Network**, and **Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)**.
 
• It serves as a primary troubleshooting tool to **Force Quit** or **End Task** for applications that have become unresponsive or are consuming excessive resources.
 
• In the **Windows 11 (version 22H2)** update, the tool was redesigned with a new hamburger menu, **Efficiency Mode**, and a layout that matches the **Fluent Design** system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Control Panel:**

 
 
• The **Control Panel** is a legacy component of **Microsoft Windows** which provides the ability to view and change system settings.
 
• It contains applets for managing **User Accounts**, **Hardware and Sound**, **Programs**, and **System Security**.
 
• There is no direct three-key global shortcut like **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** for the **Control Panel**; users typically open it via the **Start Menu** or by typing "control" in the **Run** dialog box (**Win + R**).
 
 
 
• **Settings App:**
 
 
• The **Settings** app is the modern interface for configuring the operating system, introduced in **Windows 8** and significantly expanded in **Windows 10** and **Windows 11**.
 
• The dedicated keyboard shortcut to open **Settings** in **Windows 11** is **Windows Key + I**.
 
• It is designed to eventually replace the legacy **Control Panel** for most administrative tasks.
 
 
 
• **File Explorer:**
 
 
• **File Explorer**, previously known as **Windows Explorer**, is the file management application used to browse folders and files.
 
• The standard keyboard shortcut to launch **File Explorer** is **Windows Key + E**.
 
• In **Windows 11**, **File Explorer** features a tabbed interface, similar to a web browser, allowing multiple folders to be open in a single window.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Ctrl + Alt + Del and Ctrl + Shift + Esc:**

 
 
• **Ctrl + Alt + Del** is a "Secure Attention Sequence" that interrupts the OS and opens a security options screen (Lock, Switch User, Sign out, Task Manager).
 
• **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** is a direct command handled by the **Explorer.exe** process to launch the **Task Manager** instantly.
 
 
 
• **Startup Apps Management:**
 
 
• The **Task Manager** contains a **Startup** tab (re-labeled as **Startup apps** in Windows 11) that allows users to enable or disable programs that run automatically when the computer boots up.
 
• Managing these apps is crucial for improving the **Boot Time** of the system.
 
 
 
• **Efficiency Mode:**
 
 
• A unique feature in **Windows 11** Task Manager is **Efficiency Mode** (formerly Eco Mode), which reduces the process priority and improves power efficiency for background tasks, particularly useful for **Laptop** users to conserve **Battery Life**.

questions.question: The abbreviation ASCII is a critical computer standard used worldwide. The letter C in ASCII stands for Code, indicating that ASCII is a standard system for assigning a unique numerical value to every single character, which is known as a character _________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**encoding scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ASCII** stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**, which is a character **encoding scheme** used to represent text in computers and other communication devices.
 
• The letter **C** in the acronym stands for **Code**, signifying that it is a systematic set of rules used to convert information, such as letters or symbols, into a **numerical value** that a computer can process. *Hence, the statement regarding ASCII being a character encoding scheme is correct.*
 
• It was first published as a standard in **1963** by the **American Standards Association** (now known as **ANSI** - **American National Standards Institute**).
 
• The **Standard ASCII** system uses **7 bits** to represent each character, which allows for a total of **128 unique characters** (ranging from **0 to 127**).
 
• These characters include **uppercase letters** (A-Z), **lowercase letters** (a-z), **digits** (0-9), **punctuation marks**, and various **control characters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Character Encoding**: This is the process of assigning **binary values** to characters so that electronic devices can store and transmit data. Without a universal **encoding scheme**, different computer systems would be unable to communicate effectively.
 
• **Extended ASCII**: While the standard version uses **7 bits**, **Extended ASCII** uses **8 bits** (one byte). This expansion allows for **256 characters**, accommodating special characters, **mathematical symbols**, and characters from different **languages**.
 
• **Unicode and UTF-8**: In modern computing, **ASCII** has been largely superseded by **Unicode**, specifically the **UTF-8** encoding. **UTF-8** is backward compatible with **ASCII**, meaning the first **128 characters** in **Unicode** are identical to those in the **ASCII** set.
 
• **Data Representation**: Each **ASCII** character corresponds to a specific **decimal** and **hexadecimal** value. For example, the uppercase letter **'A'** is represented by the decimal number **65**, while the lowercase **'a'** is **97**, and the digit **'0'** is **48**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Control Characters**: The first **32 characters** (0–31) in the **ASCII** table are designated as **control characters**. These are non-printing characters used to control hardware devices like **printers** and **teletypewriters** (e.g., **Line Feed**, **Carriage Return**, and **Escape**).
 
• **Applications**: **ASCII** is used in **programming**, **data protocols**, and **plain text files**. Even though complex documents use **Unicode**, **ASCII** remains the fundamental building block for **source code** in languages like **C**, **Java**, and **Python**.
 
• **History**: Before **ASCII**, there was no standard way for different **mainframe computers** to talk to each other. The introduction of this **standard** in the **United States** revolutionized the **IT industry** by ensuring **interoperability** across different manufacturers.
 
• **Numerical Precision**: In **7-bit ASCII**, the binary representation of **'A'** is **01000001** (using an **8-bit** byte where the first bit is **0**). This consistency allows **network protocols** to ensure that data sent from one **location** arrives exactly as intended at the destination.

In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.

Q. Five boxes – Box-A, Box-B, Box-C, Box-D, and Box-E – have different weights.

Which box is the second heaviest?

(I) Box-C is heavier than Box-A and Box-B but lighter than Box-D.

(II) Box-E is heavier than Box-C but lighter than Box-D.

options.text: Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not
Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. Box-C is heavier than Box-A and Box-B but lighter than Box-D.

II. Box-E is heavier than Box-C but lighter than Box-D.

Analysis:

I. From Statement I → D > C > A, B, but position of E is unknown → Not sufficient.

II. From Statement II → D > E > C, but position of A and B is unknown → Not sufficient.

Using both I and II together → We get: D > E > C > A, B

So, the full order can be: D (heaviest), E (second), C, A/B (unknown order)

Thus, the second heaviest box is **E**, and only by combining both statements we can fix this position uniquely.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

questions.question: Amit invested equal amounts at simple interest and compound interest, compounded annually, for 2 years at the same rate of 4% per annum. In the end, he noticed a difference of ₹52 between the two interests earned. What was the amount (in ₹) invested in each case?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, difference between CI and SI = P × (r ÷ 100)²

Given difference = 52 and r = 4%

⇒ 52 = P × (4 ÷ 100)² = P × 16 ÷ 10000

⇒ P = 52 × 10000 ÷ 16

**∴ Answer = 32500**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate = 4% per annum, Time = 2 years, Difference between CI and SI = 52

**Formula used:**

SI = P × r × t ÷ 100

CI = P × (1 + r ÷ 100)t − P

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 2 years = P × 4 × 2 ÷ 100 = 8P ÷ 100

⇒ CI for 2 years = P × (1 + 4 ÷ 100)² − P

⇒ = P × (1.04)² − P = P × 1.0816 − P = 0.0816P

⇒ Difference = CI − SI = 0.0816P − 0.08P = 0.0016P

⇒ 0.0016P = 52

⇒ P = 52 ÷ 0.0016 = 32500

**∴ The correct answer is 32500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI (2 years)

CI − SI = P × (r ÷ 100)² — direct formula for quick calculation

Compound Interest Formula

CI = P × (1 + r ÷ 100)ⁿ − P

Simple Interest Formula

SI = P × r × t ÷ 100

Exam Trick

For small rates and 2 years, directly use difference formula to save time

• **The Role of the USDA:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

Let number = 0.2666...

⇒ Split = 0.2 + 0.0666...

⇒ 0.0666... = 1/15

⇒ Total = 1/5 + 1/15 = (3 + 1)/15 = 4/15

**∴ Answer = 4/15**

x = 0.2666...

Multiplication method to remove recurring part

⇒ 10x = 2.6666...

⇒ 100x = 26.6666...

⇒ Subtract: 100x − 10x = 26.6666... − 2.6666...

⇒ 90x = 24

⇒ x = 24 ÷ 90

⇒ x = 4 ÷ 15

**∴ The correct answer is 4/15.**

questions.question: Which amendment made it constitutionally mandatory for municipalities to prepare “District Planning Committees” and “Metropolitan Planning Committees”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**74th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **74th Constitutional Amendment Act**, passed in **1992**, granted constitutional status and protection to **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)** or **Municipalities**.
 
• Under **Article 243ZD** of the Constitution, it is mandatory for every state to constitute a **District Planning Committee (DPC)** at the district level to consolidate the plans prepared by the **Panchayats** and the **Municipalities** in the district and to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole. ***Hence, the requirement for District Planning Committees is correct.***
 
• Under **Article 243ZE**, the Act provides for the constitution of a **Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC)** in every **Metropolitan area** (an area having a population of **10 lakhs** or more) to prepare a draft development plan for the metropolitan area as a whole. ***Hence, the requirement for Metropolitan Planning Committees is correct.***
 
• This amendment added a new **Part IX-A** to the Constitution of India, titled '**The Municipalities**', consisting of provisions from **Articles 243-P to 243-ZG**.
 
• The Act also added the **12th Schedule** to the Constitution, which contains **18 functional items** that fall under the purview of municipalities, such as **urban planning**, **regulation of land use**, and **water supply**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **73rd Amendment Act (1992):**

 
 
• This amendment granted constitutional status to **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** for rural local self-government.
 
• It added **Part IX** and the **11th Schedule** to the Constitution, covering **29 functional items** for Panchayats.
 
• While it deals with **District Planning** via integration, the specific mandate for **Metropolitan Planning Committees** is unique to the **74th Amendment**.
 
 
 
• **97th Amendment Act (2011):**
 
 
• This amendment gave constitutional status and protection to **Co-operative Societies**.
 
• It inserted **Part IX-B** into the Constitution and made the right to form co-operative societies a **Fundamental Right** under **Article 19**.
 
• It also added a new **Directive Principle of State Policy (Article 43-B)** regarding the promotion of co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **102nd Amendment Act (2018):**
 
 
• This amendment provided constitutional status to the **National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)**.
 
• It inserted **Article 338B** and **Article 342A** into the Constitution of India.
 
• The **NCBC** was previously a statutory body under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Composition of District Planning Committees (DPC):** The **74th Amendment** specifies that **four-fifths (80%)** of the members of a **DPC** should be elected by the elected members of the **District Panchayat** and **Municipalities** in the district from amongst themselves.
 
• **Composition of Metropolitan Planning Committees (MPC):** The Act stipulates that **two-thirds (66.6%)** of the members of an **MPC** should be elected by the elected members of the **Municipalities** and **Chairpersons of the Panchayats** in the metropolitan area from amongst themselves.
 
• **Effective Date:** The **74th Amendment Act** came into force on **June 1, 1993**, marking a significant shift towards **democratic decentralization** in urban India.
 
• **Types of Municipalities:** The Act provides for three types of municipalities: **Nagar Panchayat** for transitional areas, **Municipal Council** for smaller urban areas, and **Municipal Corporation** for larger urban areas.

All crabs are bats. All bats are wigs. All wigs are dogs.

**Conclusions:**

(I) All crabs are dogs.

(II) Some dogs are bats.
questions.solution:

questions.question: P sells an item to Q at 77% profit. Q sells the same item to R at 50% loss. If R paid ₹ 2655 for the item, then at what price (in ₹) is the item purchased by P?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take ratio method

P → Q at 77% profit ⇒ multiply by 177/100

Q → R at 50% loss ⇒ multiply by 1/2

Net factor = 177/100 × 1/2 = 177/200

⇒ CP of P = 2655 × 200 / 177 = 3000

**∴ Answer = 3000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P sells to Q at 77% profit, Q sells to R at 50% loss, R pays = 2655

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + profit/100), SP = CP × (1 − loss/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP of P = x

⇒ SP of P (price for Q) = x × 177/100

⇒ CP of Q = x × 177/100

⇒ SP of Q (price for R) = (x × 177/100) × 1/2

⇒ SP of Q = x × 177/200

⇒ Given x × 177/200 = 2655

⇒ x = 2655 × 200 / 177

⇒ x = 3000

**∴ The correct answer is 3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Profit & Loss

Overall effect = multiply individual profit/loss factors

Profit Formula

SP = CP × (1 + profit/100)

Loss Formula

SP = CP × (1 − loss/100)

Shortcut Tip

Convert percentages into fractions and multiply directly

questions.question: On 21 December 2025, President Droupadi Murmu approved the Viksit Bharat—Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Bill, 2025, enhancing rural wage employment guarantee to which of the following days in a financial year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**125 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Viksit Bharat—Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Bill, 2025**, was introduced to modernize and expand the scope of rural employment in India.
 
• President **Droupadi Murmu** provided her official assent to this bill on **21 December 2025**, following its passage in both houses of Parliament during the winter session.
 
• A central provision of this legislation is the significant enhancement of the guaranteed wage employment period. It increases the minimum entitlement from the previous **100 days** to **125 days** for every rural household in a **financial year**.
 
• The bill aims to provide a more robust safety net for **rural workers**, addressing the evolving economic needs and ensuring that the "**Right to Work**" is more substantial under the **Viksit Bharat @ 2047** vision.
 
• This mission specifically targets **unorganized workers** in **rural areas**, focusing on those who rely on manual labor for their primary source of income during lean agricultural seasons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transition from MGNREGA:**

 
 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, enacted in **2005**, was the predecessor to this mission. It originally provided **100 days** of work to at least one member of every **rural household**.
 
• The new **VB–G RAM G** framework integrates **asset creation** with **skill development**, moving beyond mere manual labor to "**Ajeevika**" (Livelihood) enhancement.
 
 
 
• **Viksit Bharat @ 2047 Vision:**
 
 
• This mission is a core component of the **Viksit Bharat** (Developed India) roadmap. It aims to eliminate **rural poverty** and ensure **inclusive growth** by the **100th year** of India's **Independence**.
 
• The focus is on building **climate-resilient** infrastructure, such as **check dams**, **canal lining**, and **rural roads**, which contribute to long-term **village development**.
 
 
 
• **Administrative and Financial Structure:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Rural Development** acts as the nodal agency for the implementation of this mission across all **states and Union Territories**.
 
• Funding for the **125 days** of employment is shared between the **Central Government** and the **State Governments**, with the Center bearing the majority of the **wage cost**.
 
• Payments are strictly mandated through **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**, linked to **Aadhaar-based** payment systems to ensure **transparency** and eliminate **leakages**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Application and Demand:**

 
 
• Workers can apply for work under this mission at their local **Gram Panchayat** office. The law mandates that work must be provided within **15 days** of the demand; otherwise, an **unemployment allowance** must be paid by the state.
 
 
 
• **Geographic and Demographic Focus:**
 
 
• While the mission is **nationwide**, special emphasis and additional **budgetary allocations** are provided for **Aspirational Districts** and **tribal regions** to bridge the **socio-economic** gap.
 
• The scheme maintains a **reservation** or priority for **women**, mandating that at least **one-third** of the beneficiaries must be **female workers** to promote **gender equality** in the **rural workforce**.

questions.question: Which of the following countries is the youngest country in terms of the lowest median age for the year 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Niger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Niger** is consistently ranked as the country with the lowest median age globally. For the year **2024**, the estimated median age in **Niger** is approximately **14.9 years**. This demographic reality indicates that half of the nation's population is under the age of **15**. *Hence, the statement regarding Niger is correct.*
 
• The primary driver for this extremely low median age is the **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)**. **Niger** has the highest fertility rate in the world, with an average of **6.7 to 6.8 children per woman** as per recent **World Bank** and **United Nations** data. *Hence, this reinforces why it remains the youngest country.*
 
• **Palestine**, particularly the **Gaza Strip**, has a very young population with a median age of approximately **19.6 years** in **2024**. While it is one of the youngest territories in the **Middle East**, it is significantly "older" than Niger. *Hence, the statement regarding Palestine as the youngest in this list is incorrect.*
 
• **Afghanistan** has a median age of roughly **18.4 years** in **2024**. High birth rates and a relatively low life expectancy contribute to its youthful profile, yet it does not reach the level of youthfulness found in the **Sahel** region of **Africa**. *Hence, the statement regarding Afghanistan is incorrect.*
 
• **Iraq** possesses a median age of approximately **21.2 years** as of **2024** projections. While it faces a "youth bulge" that impacts its economy and social services, it is the oldest among the four options provided. *Hence, the statement regarding Iraq is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Median Age Definition:** The **median age** is a single index that summarizes the age distribution of a population. It is the age that divides a population into two numerically equal groups; that is, half the people are younger than this age and half are older.
 
• **Geographic Concentration of Youth:** The majority of the world's youngest countries are located in **Sub-Saharan Africa**. Countries like **Mali**, **Chad**, **Angola**, and **Uganda** all have median ages below **17 years**, driven by high birth rates and improvements in **infant mortality** rates that allow more children to survive into adolescence.
 
• **Global Contrast:** In sharp contrast to **Niger**, developed nations such as **Japan**, **Italy**, and **Monaco** have the highest median ages, often exceeding **47 to 50 years**. This is due to low fertility rates and high life expectancy, leading to an **aging population** crisis.
 
• **Demographic Dividend:** A low median age presents both a challenge and an opportunity known as the **demographic dividend**. If a country can provide education and jobs for its large youth population, it can see rapid economic growth; otherwise, it may face **socio-political instability**.
 
• **Data Sources:** These demographic statistics are tracked annually by organizations such as the **United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)**, the **CIA World Factbook**, and the **World Bank** to help governments plan for **healthcare**, **education**, and **infrastructure** needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of Life Expectancy:** While **Niger** is the youngest, it also faces challenges with **life expectancy**, which is approximately **63 years**. The combination of many births and relatively shorter lifespans keeps the median age low.
 
• **Urbanization Trends:** In countries like **Iraq** and **Afghanistan**, urbanization is slowly increasing the median age as urban families tend to have fewer children compared to **rural** counterparts. **Niger** remains heavily **agrarian** and rural, which sustains higher fertility traditions.
 
• **Social Indicators:** **Literacy rates** and **female education** are inversely correlated with the median age. In **Niger**, the low literacy rate among women is a significant factor in the sustained high **Total Fertility Rate**.

questions.question: If A's salary is 130% more than that of B, then by how much percent is B's salary less than that of A (correct to 2 decimal places)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let B = 100

A = 130% more ⇒ 230

Difference = 130

% less of B from A = (130 / 230) × 100 ≈ 56.52%

**∴ Answer = 56.52%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A's salary is 130% more than B's salary

**Formula used:**

Percentage = (Difference ÷ Base) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let B = 100

⇒ A = 100 + 130 = 230

⇒ Difference = A − B = 230 − 100 = 130

⇒ % less of B compared to A = (130 ÷ 230) × 100

⇒ = 56.52%

**∴ The correct answer is 56.52%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

New value = Original × (1 + increase/100)

Percentage Decrease

Decrease % is calculated on the larger value when comparing reduction

Important Tip

Always check the base value while calculating percentage difference

Ratio Insight

If A:B = 230:100, then % difference uses A as base for “less than”

questions.question: Which language was predominantly used by Amir Khusrau in his literary compositions during the Delhi Sultanate period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Persian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amir Khusrau** (**1253–1325 AD**) was a legendary Sufi musician, poet, and scholar who lived during the era of the **Delhi Sultanate**. He was a prolific writer who primarily used **Persian** as his literary medium, which was the official and court language of the **Sultanate** at the time.
 
• He is often referred to as the "**Parrot of India**" (**Tuti-e-Hind**) and is considered the "**Father of Urdu Literature**" for his early contributions to **Hindavi**, though his major historical and poetic works were composed in **Persian**.
 
• Khusrau served in the royal courts of more than **seven** different rulers of the **Delhi Sultanate**, including **Ghiyas ud din Balban**, **Jalaluddin Khalji**, **Alauddin Khalji**, and **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.
 
• His famous literary works in **Persian** include **Khazain-ul-Futuh** (a prose work on the victories of **Alauddin Khalji**), **Tughlaq Nama** (detailing the reign of the **Tughlaq dynasty**), and **Nuh Sipihr** (The Nine Skies), which describes India's culture and environment.
 
• While he also wrote in **Hindavi** (a mixture of **Braj Bhasha** and **Khari Boli**) to reach the masses, **Persian** remained his dominant language for formal, academic, and courtly documentation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Delhi Sultanate** (**1206–1526 AD**): During this period, **Persian** was established as the **administrative and literary language** of Northern India. This led to a significant fusion of **Persian**, **Arabic**, and **Turkic** elements with local Indian dialects.
 
• **Musical Contributions**: **Amir Khusrau** is credited with introducing the **Qawwali** style of music and is traditionally believed to have invented or modified instruments like the **Sitar** and the **Tabla** by blending **Persian** and Indian musical traditions.
 
• **Sufism**: He was the most beloved disciple of the famous **Chishti** saint, **Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya**. His poetry often reflected deep **mysticism** and spiritual devotion, further popularizing **Sufi** thought in the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• **Linguistic Legacy**: He played a vital role in the development of **Sabk-i-Hindi** (the Indian style of **Persian** poetry), which influenced generations of poets in **India** and **Central Asia**.
 
• **Khari Boli**: Khusrau is often cited as the first poet to use **Khari Boli**, which eventually evolved into modern **Hindi** and **Urdu**, showing his versatility across both **Persian** and local vernaculars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location**: **Amir Khusrau** was born in **Patiyali** (modern-day **Kasganj district** of **Uttar Pradesh**, **India**) in the year **1253**.
 
• **Names and Titles**: His birth name was **Ab'ul Hasan Yamin al-Din Khusrau**. He was highly regarded for his intellect and was honored with titles by various **Sultans** for his poetic brilliance.
 
• **Specific Dates**: His work **Khazain-ul-Futuh** was completed around **1311 AD**, providing a critical primary source for the **military campaigns** of the **Khalji dynasty** in **South India**.
 
• **Cultural Impact**: He was one of the first scholars to compare **Indian culture** and languages favorably against **Arabic** and **Persian**, expressing great pride in his **Indian** identity in his work **Nuh Sipihr** (written in **1318 AD**).

questions.question: The price of each article of type P, Q, and R is ₹280, ₹180 and ₹120, respectively. Subrata buys articles of each type in the ratio 3 : 2 : 3 for ₹6,240. How many articles of type Q did he purchase?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio = 3 : 2 : 3 ⇒ total parts = 8

Cost of 1 set = (3×280 + 2×180 + 3×120)

= 840 + 360 + 360 = 1560

Number of sets = 6240 ÷ 1560 = 4

Q articles = 2 × 4 = 8

**∴ Answer = 8**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Prices: P = 280, Q = 180, R = 120; Ratio = 3 : 2 : 3; Total cost = 6240

**Formula used:**

Total cost = (quantity × price)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let quantities be 3x, 2x, 3x

⇒ Total cost = 3x×280 + 2x×180 + 3x×120

⇒ = 840x + 360x + 360x

⇒ = 1560x

⇒ 1560x = 6240

⇒ x = 4

⇒ Quantity of Q = 2x = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

Ratio Method

Quantities in ratio can be taken as multiples of a variable like x.

Cost Formula

Total cost = Sum of (price × quantity)

Unit Method

Find cost of one ratio set, then scale up to total.

Proportion Concept

If total cost is known, find multiplier to get actual quantities.

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a room are 20m, 10m and 6m, respectively. If the rate of painting the four walls and the ceiling of the room is ₹15/square metre, then find the total cost.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of 4 walls = 2h(l + b) = 2×6(20 + 10) = 12×30 = 360 m²

Ceiling area = l×b = 20×10 = 200 m²

Total area = 360 + 200 = 560 m²

Cost = 560 × 15 = 8400

**∴ Answer = ₹8400**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length = 20 m, Breadth = 10 m, Height = 6 m, Rate = ₹15/m²

**Formula used:**

Area of four walls = 2h(l + b), Ceiling area = l×b

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of four walls = 2×6×(20 + 10)

⇒ = 12×30 = 360 m²

⇒ Ceiling area = 20×10 = 200 m²

⇒ Total area = 360 + 200 = 560 m²

⇒ Total cost = 560 × 15

⇒ = 8400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Four Walls

Area = 2h(l + b), also called lateral surface area of a cuboid.

Ceiling Area

Ceiling is a rectangle ⇒ Area = l × b

Total Painting Area

Total area = Area of four walls + ceiling

Cost Formula

Cost = Area × Rate per unit area

questions.question: Under the Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025, if an obligated entity fails to meet targets, then environmental compensation is linked to carbon credit prices. The compensation for shortfall is:

options.text: Equal to the average traded price of carbon credit certificates
Three times the average traded price of carbon credit certificates
A fixed penalty per tonne decided by SPCBs
Twice the average traded price of carbon credit certificates

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Twice the average traded price of carbon credit certificates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** notified the **Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025**, under the framework of the **Energy Conservation Act, 2001** and its **2022 amendment**.
 
• These rules are designed to mandate **obligated entities** in sectors like **iron, steel, cement, and petrochemicals** to reduce their **greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity** over a specified **compliance period**.
 
• If an obligated entity fails to achieve the assigned target, it is required to purchase **Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs)** from the market to bridge the gap; failure to do so results in **environmental compensation**.
 
• The rules explicitly state that the **environmental compensation** for the shortfall shall be **twice the average traded price** of the **Carbon Credit Certificates** during the relevant compliance cycle. *Hence, the statement regarding the penalty being twice the price is correct.*
 
• This **financial penalty** mechanism is intended to create a strong economic deterrent against non-compliance and to encourage investment in **cleaner technologies** and **decarbonization**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS):** This is India's domestic **carbon market** framework launched in **2023** to incentivize **GHG reduction**. It allows for the **trading** of certificates between entities that exceed their targets and those that fall short.
 
• **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE):** The **BEE** acts as the **Administrator** for the carbon market. It is responsible for determining **emission targets**, monitoring **performance**, and issuing **Carbon Credit Certificates**.
 
• **Obligated Entities:** These are **designated consumers** under the **Energy Conservation Act** who are required to comply with **energy consumption** and **emission intensity** norms. This includes major industries that contribute significantly to India's **carbon footprint**.
 
• **Greenhouse Gas Emission Intensity:** This refers to the **amount of GHG emissions** produced per unit of **output or activity** (e.g., tonnes of CO2 per tonne of steel produced). Reducing intensity allows for **industrial growth** while minimizing **environmental impact**.
 
• **Compliance Cycle:** The period during which an entity's **emissions** are monitored against its **targets**. This is typically aligned with the **financial year** or a specific **three-year cycle** as determined by the **Central Government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Authority:** The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** is often tasked with the **collection** of **environmental compensation** and the **management** of the resulting funds, which are typically used for **environmental restoration**.
 
• **Verification Mechanism:** The **emissions data** provided by the entities must be **audited** and **verified** by **Accredited Carbon Verifiers** to ensure **transparency** and **authenticity** in the carbon market.
 
• **International Context:** These rules help **India** meet its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement**, aiming for **Net Zero** emissions by the **year 2070**.
 
• **Price Determination:** The **average traded price** is calculated based on the **market transactions** recorded on the **Indian Carbon Exchange** or other designated **trading platforms** throughout the **compliance year**.

questions.question: Which combination of symptoms is the most common characteristic of influenza in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fever, cough, and body aches**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Influenza**, commonly known as the **flu**, is a highly contagious respiratory illness caused by **influenza viruses** that infect the nose, throat, and sometimes the lungs.
 
• The most common and characteristic symptoms of **influenza** include a **sudden onset of high fever** (often **100°F or 38°C** or higher), a **dry cough**, **sore throat**, and **significant body aches** or **myalgia**. ***Hence, the combination in Option C is correct.***
 
• Unlike the **common cold**, which tends to develop gradually, **influenza** symptoms typically appear **abruptly** and are much more severe, often leaving the patient feeling extremely **fatigued** or exhausted for several days.
 
• **Systemic symptoms** like **headache** and **chills** frequently accompany the **respiratory symptoms**, distinguishing it from local allergic reactions or simple physical exertion.
 
• While **gastrointestinal symptoms** like **vomiting** and **diarrhea** can occur, they are much more common in **children** than in **adults** and are not the primary diagnostic hallmark of **respiratory influenza**. ***Hence, Option D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Influenza Viruses:**

 
 
• **Influenza A**: These are the only **flu viruses** known to cause **pandemics** (global outbreaks). They can infect both **humans** and **animals** (such as birds and pigs). Notable strains include **H1N1** and **H3N2**.
 
• **Influenza B**: These viruses generally infect only **humans** and are responsible for **seasonal epidemics**. They do not cause pandemics.
 
• **Influenza C**: These viruses cause **mild respiratory illness** and are not thought to cause large-scale epidemics.
 
• **Influenza D**: These primarily affect **cattle** and are not known to infect or cause illness in people.
 
 
 
• **Transmission and Prevention:**
 
 
• The virus is spread primarily through **respiratory droplets** expelled when an infected person **coughs**, **sneezes**, or talks. These droplets can land in the mouths or noses of people who are nearby (usually within **6 feet**).
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** recommends annual **vaccination** as the most effective way to prevent the disease, especially for **high-risk groups** like **elderly individuals**, **pregnant women**, and **healthcare workers**.
 
• **Antiviral medications**, such as **Oseltamivir** (Tamiflu) or **Zanamivir**, can be used to treat the flu and may reduce the duration of symptoms if taken within **48 hours** of onset.
 
 
 
• **Differentiation from Other Conditions:**
 
 
• **Rash, itching, and swelling**: These are typically signs of **allergic reactions** (anaphylaxis) or **dermatological conditions** rather than a viral respiratory infection. ***Hence, Option A is incorrect.***
 
• **Chest pain and palpitations**: While severe flu can lead to **complications** like **myocarditis**, these are primarily indicators of **cardiac issues** or **angina**. ***Hence, Option B is incorrect.***
 
• **Incubation Period**: The time from exposure to the virus to the appearance of symptoms is usually **1 to 4 days**, with an average of **2 days**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Complications:** If not managed, **influenza** can lead to severe **secondary infections** such as **pneumonia**, **bronchitis**, **sinus infections**, and **ear infections**.
 
• **High-Risk Populations:** Children under **5 years**, adults over **65 years**, and individuals with **chronic medical conditions** (like **asthma**, **diabetes**, or **heart disease**) are at a higher risk of developing **complications**.
 
• **Global Impact:** Seasonal **influenza** causes approximately **3 to 5 million** cases of severe illness and about **290,000 to 650,000** respiratory deaths annually worldwide, according to **WHO** data.

questions.question: Which new weapon led to Mangal Pandey’s agitation as a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Enfield rifle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary cause of **Mangal Pandey’s** agitation was the introduction of the **Enfield P-53 rifle**, which replaced the older **Brown Bess musket** in the **British East India Company's** army.
 
• The **Enfield rifle** used a new type of **cartridge** that was rumored to be greased with **cow and pig fat**. This was highly offensive to the religious sentiments of **Hindu** and **Muslim** sepoys, as cows are sacred in **Hinduism** and pigs are considered haram in **Islam**.
 
• To load the **Enfield rifle**, a soldier had to **bite off the end** of the greased cartridge before pouring the gunpowder into the muzzle. This direct contact with the fat-laden grease was seen as a deliberate attempt by the **British** to defile the soldiers' religions.
 
• On **March 29, 1857**, **Mangal Pandey**, a sepoy of the **34th Bengal Native Infantry (BNI)** stationed at **Barrackpore** (near **Kolkata**), revolted against his **British officers**, marking the prelude to the **Revolt of 1857**.
 
• During the incident, **Mangal Pandey** attacked **Lieutenant Baugh** and **Sergeant-Major Hewson**. He was subsequently **arrested**, **court-martialed**, and **hanged** on **April 8, 1857**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **34th Bengal Native Infantry:** This was the specific regiment where **Mangal Pandey** served. Following the uprising in **March 1857**, the entire regiment was **disbanded** by the **British** as a collective punishment for failing to restrain or arrest **Pandey** during his rebellion.
 
• **Revolt of 1857:** Often termed the **First War of Indian Independence** or the **Sepoy Mutiny**, it was a massive uprising against **British East India Company** rule. While the **Enfield rifle** was the **immediate cause**, deep-seated grievances regarding **land revenue**, **annexation policies** (like the **Doctrine of Lapse**), and **social reforms** also played major roles.
 
• **Lord Canning:** He was the **Governor-General of India** during the **1857 Revolt**. He served from **1856 to 1862** and became the **first Viceroy of India** after the **Government of India Act 1858** transferred power from the Company to the **British Crown**.
 
• **Brown Bess Musket:** This was the standard-issue **muzzle-loading smoothbore musket** used by the **British Army** for over a century before the **Enfield rifle** was introduced. Unlike the **Enfield**, it did not utilize the controversial **greased cartridges**.
 
• **Matchlock Gun:** These were older types of **firearms** that used a **slow-burning match** to ignite the **gunpowder**. By **1857**, they were obsolete for regular **British infantry** use and were replaced by **flintlocks** and later **percussion cap** rifles like the **Enfield**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographic Spread:** Although the agitation started in **Barrackpore**, the main rebellion broke out in **Meerut** on **May 10, 1857**, when soldiers of the **3rd Native Cavalry** refused to use the **Enfield cartridges**.
 
• **Mangal Pandey's Legacy:** He is hailed as one of the **first martyrs** of the **Indian freedom struggle**. In **1984**, the **Government of India** issued a **postage stamp** in his honor to commemorate his bravery and sacrifice.
 
• **Technological Shift:** The **Enfield Pattern 1853 Rifle-Musket** was a **rifled** firearm, meaning it had **grooves** inside the barrel to spin the bullet, making it much more **accurate** and **longer-ranged** than the smoothbore **Brown Bess**. However, this **technological advancement** became the catalyst for political upheaval due to cultural insensitivity.
 
• **British Response:** The **British** initially tried to calm the sepoys by allowing them to grease their own cartridges with **vegetable oil** or **wax**, but the **mistrust** was already too deep-seated, leading to the **total breakdown** of authority across **Northern** and **Central India**.

questions.question: The Garo, Khasi, Jaintia, and Naga Hills, which run almost east–west, are connected to which hill chain that extends in a north–south direction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizo and Rakhine Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Garo**, **Khasi**, **Jaintia**, and **Naga Hills** are part of the physiographic division of **Northeast India**. While the **Garo**, **Khasi**, and **Jaintia** hills primarily form the **Meghalaya Plateau**, the **Naga Hills** are part of the **Purvanchal** range.
 
• The hill ranges of **Meghalaya** (Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia) run in an almost **East-West** direction, creating a high-altitude barrier. **Hence, the statement regarding their east-west orientation is correct.**
 
• These east-west trending hills are connected to the **Purvanchal Range**, which takes a sharp southward turn after the **Dihang gorge**. This southward extension continues as a series of **North-South** trending hills. **Hence, the statement regarding the connection to a north-south chain is correct.**
 
• The specific **North-South** extensions identified in the correct option are the **Mizo Hills** (formerly known as **Lushai Hills**) located in **India** and the **Rakhine Hills** (also known as **Arakan Yoma**) located in **Myanmar**.
 
• The **Purvanchal** hills are composed of strong **sandstones**, which are **sedimentary rocks**. They are covered with dense forests and run as parallel ranges and valleys.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mizo Hills (Lushai Hills):** Located in the state of **Mizoram**, these hills are part of the **Patkai** range system. The highest point in the Mizo Hills is **Phawngpui**, also known as the **Blue Mountain**, with an elevation of **2,157 meters**.
 
• **Rakhine Hills (Arakan Yoma):** This is a massive mountain range in western **Myanmar** that runs **North-South** for approximately **950 kilometers**. It acts as a natural barrier between **Myanmar** and the **Indian Subcontinent**.
 
• **Vindhya and Satpura Hills:** These are located in **Central India**. The **Vindhya Range** runs north of the **Narmada River**, while the **Satpura Range** runs south of it. They are **not** connected to the **Northeastern** hill systems.
 
• **Nilgiri Hills:** Located in **South India** at the junction of the **Western Ghats** and **Eastern Ghats** in the states of **Tamil Nadu**, **Karnataka**, and **Kerala**. It is geographically isolated from the **Purvanchal** system.
 
• **Meghalaya Plateau Structure:** Although located in the **Northeast**, the **Garo-Khasi-Jaintia** hills are geologically an extension of the **Peninsular Plateau** (specifically the **Chotanagpur Plateau**), separated by the **Malda Fault** in **West Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Patkai Bum:** These are the hills located in the northernmost part of the **Purvanchal**, forming the border between **India** (**Arunachal Pradesh**) and **Myanmar**.
 
• **Mount Saramati:** This is the highest peak in the **Naga Hills**, reaching a height of **3,841 meters**. It stays snow-clad during **winter** and is located on the **Nagaland**-**Myanmar** border.
 
• **Barail Range:** This range acts as a link between the **Naga Hills** and the **Jaintia Hills**. It is the highest hill range in **Assam**.
 
• **Climate Impact:** The orientation of the **Garo**, **Khasi**, and **Jaintia Hills** is responsible for trapping the **Southwest Monsoon** winds, leading to **heavy rainfall** in places like **Mawsynram** and **Cherrapunji**, which are among the wettest places on **Earth**.
 
• **Purvanchal States:** The **Purvanchal** range spans several states including **Arunachal Pradesh**, **Nagaland**, **Manipur**, and **Mizoram**.

questions.question: What law, as of December 2025, requires intermediaries to act against unlawful and harmful online content affecting children in India?

options.text: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021** were notified on **25th February 2021** by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** under the powers conferred by **Section 87** of the **Information Technology Act, 2000**.
 
• Under **Rule 3(1)(b)**, intermediaries are mandated to perform **due diligence**, which includes informing users not to host, display, or upload any information that is harmful to **children**. This ensures a safe digital environment for minors in **India**.
 
• The rules specifically require intermediaries to take down or disable access to content that depicts **Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM)** or any sexually explicit content within **24 hours** of receiving a complaint from an individual or a person authorized by them.
 
• It distinguishes between ordinary intermediaries and **Significant Social Media Intermediaries (SSMIs)**, which are platforms having more than **50 lakh** (5 million) registered users in **India**. These **SSMIs** have stricter compliance requirements, including the appointment of a **Chief Compliance Officer**, a **Nodal Contact Person**, and a **Resident Grievance Officer**.
 
• The **2021 Rules** represent a shift towards **accountability**, requiring intermediaries to provide a **Grievance Redressal Mechanism** where users can report violations, including those affecting the safety and dignity of **children**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Section 67B of the IT Act, 2000**: This specific section of the principal **Act** prescribes stringent punishment, including imprisonment for a **term** of up to **five years** for the first conviction, for publishing or transmitting material depicting **children** in sexually explicit acts in electronic form.
 
• **Section 79 of the Information Technology Act**: This provides "**Safe Harbour**" protection to intermediaries, exempting them from liability for third-party content. However, this protection is conditional upon the intermediary following the **due diligence** requirements specified in the **2021 Rules**.
 
• **POCSO Act, 2012**: The **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act** is the primary legislation in **India** designed to protect **children** (defined as persons below the **age** of **18 years**) from sexual abuse. It works in tandem with the **IT Rules** to prosecute digital crimes against minors.
 
• **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023**: This **Act** imposes additional obligations on data fiduciaries regarding **children's data**. It prohibits processing that is likely to cause a detrimental effect on the well-being of a **child** and mandates verifiable parental consent for users under **18 years**.
 
• **National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)**: This is the statutory body established under the **CPCR Act, 2005**, which monitors the implementation of laws related to **child** safety, including their protection in the digital space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC)**: Introduced via an amendment in **October 2022**, the **GAC** allows users to appeal against the decisions of an intermediary's **Grievance Officer**. This provides an additional layer of oversight for content moderation decisions.
 
• **Content Removal Timelines**: While general complaints must be acknowledged within **24 hours** and resolved within **15 days**, the rules emphasize "expeditious removal" for sensitive content involving **children** or the modesty of individuals.
 
• **Rule 4(2) - Traceability**: For messaging intermediaries, the rules require the identification of the **first originator** of information if ordered by a court or competent authority, primarily to prevent the spread of **CSAM** and threats to **national security**.
 
• **Compliance Reports**: **SSMIs** are required to publish **monthly compliance reports** detailing the number of complaints received and the specific actions taken, ensuring transparency in how they handle harmful online content.

 Class Interval

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mode = 36 lies in class 30−40 ⇒ modal class

Use formula idea: Mode shifts toward higher frequency

Apply relation quickly: f1 − f0 : f1 − f2 ≈ (36 − 30) : (40 − 36)

⇒ (9 − x) : (9 − 5) = 6 : 4

⇒ (9 − x)/4 = 6/4 ⇒ 9 − x = 6

⇒ x = 3

**∴ Answer = 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode = 36, class intervals with missing frequency = x in 20−30

**Formula used:**

Mode = L + [(f1 − f0) ÷ (2f1 − f0 − f2)] × h

**Calculation:**

⇒ Modal class = 30−40

⇒ L = 30, h = 10

⇒ f1 = 9, f0 = x, f2 = 5

⇒ 36 = 30 + [(9 − x) ÷ (2×9 − x − 5)] × 10

⇒ 36 = 30 + [(9 − x) ÷ (18 − x − 5)] × 10

⇒ 36 = 30 + [(9 − x) ÷ (13 − x)] × 10

⇒ 6 = [(9 − x) ÷ (13 − x)] × 10

⇒ 6(13 − x) = 10(9 − x)

⇒ 78 − 6x = 90 − 10x

⇒ 4x = 12

⇒ x = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

Class interval with highest frequency is the modal class.

Class Width

h = upper limit − lower limit

Frequency Terms

questions.question: Which wind system blows consistently from high-pressure to low-pressure areas year-round?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Planetary winds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Planetary winds**, also known as **permanent winds** or **prevailing winds**, are large-scale wind systems that blow consistently in the same direction throughout the **year** across vast regions of the **globe**.
 
• These winds originate due to the **latitudinal variation** in **atmospheric pressure**, moving from **high-pressure belts** to **low-pressure belts**.
 
• The three primary types of planetary winds are the **Trade Winds**, the **Westerlies**, and the **Polar Easterlies**.
 
• **Trade Winds** blow from the **Sub-tropical High Pressure** belt (around **30° N and S**) towards the **Equatorial Low Pressure** belt. Because of the **Coriolis Force**, they blow from the **North-East** in the **Northern Hemisphere** and the **South-East** in the **Southern Hemisphere**.
 
• **Westerlies** blow from the **Sub-tropical High Pressure** belts towards the **Sub-polar Low Pressure** belts (around **60° N and S**). They are more vigorous in the **Southern Hemisphere** due to the vast expanse of **ocean**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Local winds:** These are winds that blow over a **short period** of the **day** or **year** within a restricted area. They are often caused by **local differences** in **temperature** and **pressure**. Examples include the **Loo** (a hot, dry wind in **Northern India** and **Pakistan** during **summer**), the **Mistral** (a cold wind in **France**), and the **Chinook** (a warm wind on the eastern slopes of the **Rocky Mountains**).
 
• **Periodic winds:** These winds change their direction periodically with the change in **season** or time. The most prominent example is the **Monsoon**, which involves a complete reversal of wind direction between **summer** and **winter** in regions like **South Asia**. **Land and sea breezes** are also considered small-scale periodic winds occurring daily.
 
• **Polar winds:** Specifically called **Polar Easterlies**, these blow from the **Polar High Pressure** areas toward the **Sub-polar Low Pressure** belts. They are **cold** and **dry** winds originating from **latitudes** beyond **60°**.
 
• **Coriolis Effect:** This is an inertial force caused by the **Earth's rotation** that deflects moving air to the **right** in the **Northern Hemisphere** and to the **left** in the **Southern Hemisphere**, as described by **Ferrel's Law**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Horse Latitudes:** These are regions located at about **30° to 35° North and South** of the **Equator**, characterized by **high pressure**, **calm winds**, and **subsiding air**.
 
• **Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, and Shrieking Sixties:** These are sailors' terms for the exceptionally strong **Westerlies** found in the **Southern Hemisphere** between **40° and 60° latitude**, where there is little **landmass** to obstruct the wind flow.
 
• **Doldrums:** Also known as the **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)**, this is the **low-pressure** area around the **Equator** where the **Trade Winds** meet, often resulting in **calm weather** or **sudden storms**.
 
• The global wind circulation plays a vital role in **ocean currents** and the **redistribution of heat** from the **Equator** to the **Poles**, maintaining the **Earth's climate** balance.

questions.question: What was the Diwan-i-Riyasat under Alauddin Khilji?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Department controlling markets and prices**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji**, one of the most powerful rulers of the **Khilji Dynasty**, established the **Diwan-i-Riyasat** to implement his ambitious **Market Control Reforms**.
 
• The primary function of the **Diwan-i-Riyasat** was to regulate the **market** and ensure that all commodities were sold at the **fixed prices** determined by the **Sultan**. *Hence, the statement regarding the department controlling markets and prices is correct.*
 
• This department was headed by a high-ranking official known as the **Naib-i-Riyasat**, who exercised overall control over the **merchants** and the **supply chain**.
 
• It was mandatory for all **merchants** to register themselves with the **Diwan-i-Riyasat** before they could sell their goods in the **Delhi** markets.
 
• The department worked in coordination with the **Shahna-i-Mandi** (Market Superintendent) to prevent **hoarding**, **black marketing**, and the use of **faulty weights** or measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** (reigned **1296–1316**) introduced several administrative departments to centralize power:

 
 
• **Diwan-i-Wizarat**: This was the department of **finance** and **revenue**, headed by the **Wazir**.
 
• **Diwan-i-Arz**: This was the **military department** responsible for recruitment, training, and maintenance of the **army**.
 
• **Diwan-i-Insha**: This department handled **royal correspondence** and the drafting of **farmans** (orders).
 
• **Diwan-i-Rasalat**: This department dealt with **religious matters**, **endowments**, and **foreign affairs**.
 
 
 
• The **Department of Agriculture**, known as **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi**, was not established by Khilji but by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** to improve **land cultivation**.
 
• The **Market Control Policy** was primarily designed to maintain a massive **standing army** at a low cost, as soldiers could buy essential goods at **subsidized rates**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• To monitor the effectiveness of the **Diwan-i-Riyasat**, the **Sultan** employed a network of **spies** known as **Munhiyans** and **Barids** (intelligence officers) who reported daily on **market prices** and **fraudulent activities**.
 
• The market was categorized into three segments: **Mandi** (for grain), **Sera-i-Adl** (for manufactured goods and expensive cloth), and markets for **slaves, horses, and cattle**.
 
• The **Sultan** enforced **harsh punishments** for any merchant caught cheating; for instance, if a merchant gave **short weight**, an equivalent amount of **flesh** was cut from his body.
 
• During times of **famine** or **drought**, the **Diwan-i-Riyasat** managed the **state granaries** to ensure the continuous supply of food at **standard rates**, preventing **inflation** in the **capital city**.
 
• These reforms were so successful that prices remained **stable** throughout the **twenty-year reign** of **Alauddin Khilji**, a feat rarely matched in **medieval Indian history**.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which Indian State/UT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Taj Mahal** is an ivory-white marble mausoleum located on the southern bank of the **Yamuna River** in the city of **Agra**, which is situated in the Indian state of **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• It was commissioned in **1632** by the **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan** (reigned from **1628** to **1658**) to house the tomb of his favorite wife, **Mumtaz Mahal**; it also houses the tomb of **Shah Jahan** himself.
 
• The **Taj Mahal** was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1983** for being "the jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage."
 
• The construction project employed some **20,000 artisans** under the guidance of a board of architects led by the court architect to the emperor, **Ustad Ahmad Lahori**.
 
• It is regarded by many as the finest example of **Mughal architecture**, a style that combines elements from **Persian**, **Indian**, and **Islamic** architectural styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Architecture and Design:**

 
 
• The **main dome** of the Taj Mahal reaches a height of **73 meters** (240 feet) and is surrounded by four smaller domes.
 
• The structure is built of **white marble** sourced from **Makrana** in **Rajasthan**, which is famous for its high quality and durability.
 
• The complex includes a **mosque**, a **guest house**, and is set in **formal gardens** (Charbagh) bounded on three sides by a crenellated wall.
 
• In **2007**, the **Taj Mahal** was declared a winner of the **New Seven Wonders of the World** (2000–2007) initiative.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The construction of the mausoleum was essentially completed in **1643**, but work continued on other phases of the project for another **10 years**.
 
• The entire Taj Mahal complex is estimated to have been completed in its entirety in **1653** at a cost estimated at the time to be around **32 million rupees**.
 
• The **Mughal Empire** reached its cultural peak during the reign of **Shah Jahan**, and the Taj Mahal represents the pinnacle of this era.
 
 
 
• **Conservation and Environment:**
 
 
• To protect the monument from environmental **pollution**, the Government of India has set up the **Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ)**, a defined area of **10,400 sq km** around the monument to strictly monitor emissions.
 
• In **1996**, the **Supreme Court of India** banned the use of coal/coke in industries located within the **TTZ** and directed them to switch over to **natural gas** or relocate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Symbolism:** The Taj Mahal is widely considered a **symbol of eternal love** and is the most visited tourist destination in **India**, attracting millions of visitors annually.
 
• **Agra's Significance:** Apart from the Taj Mahal, **Agra** in **Uttar Pradesh** is also home to two other **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**: the **Agra Fort** and **Fatehpur Sikri**.
 
• **Symmetry:** The entire complex is noted for its perfect **bilateral symmetry** along a central axis, except for the tomb of **Shah Jahan**, which is placed beside **Mumtaz Mahal's** tomb, breaking the symmetry.
 
• **Materials:** Over **1,000 elephants** were used to transport building materials. Precious and semi-precious stones like **Lapis Lazuli**, **Jade**, **Crystal**, **Turquoise**, and **Sapphire** were inlaid into the white marble using the **Pietra Dura** technique.

questions.question: Which of the following terms is used for places that serve as the meeting point of two or more transport routes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Node**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the field of **Transport Geography**, a **Node** is defined as a specific location that serves as the meeting point, intersection, or junction of two or more **transport routes**.
 
• A **Node** acts as a functional unit where various paths in a system converge, allowing for the transfer of goods, people, or information from one route to another. ***Hence, the term Node is the correct answer.***
 
• In a mathematical or topological sense, these points are often referred to as **vertices**, which are connected by paths to form a comprehensive system.
 
• The **functions** of a **Node** include being a point of entry, exit, or transfer within a larger **transport network**, such as a major **city**, a **railway station**, or an **airport**.
 
• The importance of a **Node** is often measured by its **connectivity**; a higher number of **transport routes** meeting at a single point increases the strategic and economic value of that **location**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Link:**

 
 
• A **Link** is the path or connection between two **Nodes**. While a **Node** is a point, a **Link** is the segment that facilitates movement between these points.
 
• In **Graph Theory**, these are also known as **edges**. The efficiency of a **Link** is determined by its **capacity**, **speed**, and **length**.
 
 
 
• **Network:**
 
 
• A **Network** is the entire framework formed by the combination of **Nodes** and **Links**. It represents the spatial organization of a **transport system**.
 
• **Networks** can be classified as **radial**, **grid-like**, or **linear**, depending on how the **Nodes** are interconnected.
 
 
 
• **Grid:**
 
 
• A **Grid** is a specific type of **Network** structure where **transport routes** (usually roads) intersect at right angles, forming rectangular or square blocks.
 
• This **feature** is common in urban planning for **cities** like **New York** (Manhattan) or **Chandigarh** in **India** to ensure systematic **location** identification and traffic flow.
 
 
 
• **Transport Geography Concepts:**
 
 
• The study of **transportation** focuses on how **geographical** space is integrated through **infrastructure**. Key **indices** like the **Beta Index** are used to calculate the **connectivity** of a **Network** by dividing the number of **Links** by the number of **Nodes**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hub and Spoke Model:** This is a common **application** where a central **Node** (the **Hub**) handles the majority of traffic and redistributes it through **Links** (the **Spokes**) to smaller **Nodes**. **Examples** include **London Heathrow Airport** and **Dubai International Airport**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** **Nodes** with high **accessibility** often become centers of **trade** and **commerce**. Historically, **cities** located at the **intersection** of major trade routes, like **Istanbul** or **Singapore**, have flourished due to their status as vital **Nodes**.
 
• **Data and Facts:** The development of **Nodes** is often regulated by **government guidelines** and **infrastructure acts** to ensure balanced regional development. In **India**, projects like the **PM Gati Shakti** aim to create integrated **multimodal transport Nodes** to boost **logistics** efficiency.
 
• **Topology:** The spatial arrangement of **Nodes** determines the **redundancy** of a **Network**. A **Network** with many **Nodes** serving as **intersections** provides more route **options**, making the system more resilient to disruptions.

questions.question: In which type of wave do particles of the medium move parallel to the direction of wave propagation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Longitudinal wave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Longitudinal wave** is a type of **mechanical wave** where the **vibration** or **oscillation** of the **particles** of the **medium** occurs **parallel** to the **direction** in which the **wave** or **energy** travels.
 
• These waves are characterized by the formation of **compressions** and **rarefactions**. **Compressions** are regions where the **particles** are **closest together**, resulting in **high pressure** and **high density**. **Hence, the statement regarding parallel movement is correct.**
 
• **Rarefactions** are regions where the **particles** are **spread apart**, leading to **low pressure** and **low density**. This periodic **variation** in **pressure** allows the wave to **propagate** through a **material medium**. **Hence, the statement regarding wave structure is correct.**
 
• The most common **example** of a longitudinal wave is a **sound wave**. In air, sound travels as a **longitudinal wave** because the **air molecules** move **back and forth** in the **same direction** as the **sound energy**.
 
• Longitudinal waves can **propagate** through **solids**, **liquids**, and **gases**. This is because all **phases of matter** can be **compressed** and **expanded**, allowing the **transfer** of **energy** via **pressure changes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transverse Waves**:

 
 
• In these waves, the **particles** of the **medium** move **perpendicular** (at **right angles**) to the **direction** of **wave propagation**.
 
• **Examples** include **light waves**, **radio waves**, and waves produced on a **vibrating string**. Unlike longitudinal waves, they consist of **crests** (high points) and **troughs** (low points).
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Waves**:
 
 
• These are **non-mechanical waves** composed of **oscillating electric** and **magnetic fields**. They do not require a **material medium** to travel and can move through a **vacuum**.
 
• They travel at the **speed of light**, which is approximately **300,000 kilometers per second** (**3 x 10⁸ m/s**). All **electromagnetic waves** are **transverse** in nature.
 
 
 
• **Surface Waves**:
 
 
• These waves occur at the **boundary** or **interface** between two different **media**, such as **water and air**.
 
• The **particles** in a **surface wave** undergo a **circular motion**, which is a **combination** of both **longitudinal** and **transverse** movements.
 
 
 
• **Seismic Waves**:
 
 
• During an **earthquake**, **P-waves** (Primary waves) are **longitudinal** and are the **fastest** seismic waves, while **S-waves** (Secondary waves) are **transverse** and can only travel through **solids**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wavelength**: In a **longitudinal wave**, the **wavelength** is the **distance** between the **center** of one **compression** to the **center** of the **next compression**, or between two **consecutive rarefactions**.
 
• **Frequency**: This refers to the **number of compressions** or **rarefactions** that pass a **fixed point** per **unit of time** (measured in **Hertz** or **Hz**).
 
• **Medium Characteristics**: The **speed** of a longitudinal wave depends on the **elasticity** (Bulk Modulus) and the **inertia** (density) of the **medium**. For instance, **sound** travels **faster** in **solids** (like **steel** at **5960 m/s**) than in **liquids** (like **water** at **1480 m/s**) or **gases** (like **air** at **343 m/s**) because **solids** are less **compressible**.
 
• **Applications**: **Ultrasonic waves** (longitudinal waves with **frequency** above **20,000 Hz**) are used in **medical imaging** (**sonography**), **industrial cleaning**, and **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) for **underwater navigation**.

questions.question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 100% above its cost price. What percentage of discount on marked price should be allowed to gain 88%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let CP = 100

MP = 100% more ⇒ 200

Gain 88% ⇒ SP = 188

Discount = 200 − 188 = 12

Discount % = (12/200) × 100 = 6%

**∴ Answer = 6%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked price is 100% above cost price, Gain = 88%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + profit/100), Discount % = (MP − SP)/MP × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ MP = 100 + 100% of 100 = 200

⇒ SP for 88% gain = 100 × 1.88 = 188

⇒ Discount = MP − SP = 200 − 188 = 12

⇒ Discount % = (12 ÷ 200) × 100

⇒ = 6%

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price

MP = CP × (1 + markup/100)

Selling Price

SP = CP × (1 + profit/100)

Discount Formula

Discount % = (MP − SP)/MP × 100

Key Insight

Assume CP = 100 to simplify percentage problems
