questions.question: Which disease is caused specifically by a deficiency of Vitamin B1?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beri-beri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin B1**, scientifically known as **Thiamine**, is a **water-soluble vitamin** that plays a critical role in **energy metabolism** and the growth, development, and **function of cells**.
 
• A prolonged deficiency of **Thiamine** leads to a clinical condition known as **Beri-beri**. This disease primarily affects the **nervous system** and the **cardiovascular system**. ***Hence, option D is the correct statement.***
 
• There are two main types of the disease: **Wet Beri-beri**, which impacts the **heart** and circulatory system, leading to heart failure in extreme cases; and **Dry Beri-beri**, which damages the **nerves** and can lead to **muscle paralysis**.
 
• The **symptoms** of **Beri-beri** include **loss of appetite**, weakness, pain in the limbs, **shortness of breath**, and swollen feet or legs.
 
• Historically, the disease was prevalent in regions where **polished rice** (white rice) was the staple food, as the process of polishing removes the **thiamine-rich husk**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rickets:**

 
 
• This condition is caused by a deficiency of **Vitamin D**, **calcium**, or **phosphate**.
 
• It predominantly affects **children**, leading to **soft and weak bones**, which can result in skeletal deformities like **bowed legs**. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Night Blindness:**
 
 
• Scientifically termed **Nyctalopia**, this is caused by a deficiency of **Vitamin A** (**Retinol**).
 
• **Vitamin A** is essential for the production of **rhodopsin**, a pigment in the **retina** that helps us see in **low-light conditions**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Scurvy:**
 
 
• This disease results from a lack of **Vitamin C** (**Ascorbic Acid**).
 
• It is characterized by **bleeding gums**, fatigue, and **slow wound healing** because **Vitamin C** is necessary for **collagen synthesis**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Vitamins Classification:**
 
 
• Vitamins are classified into two groups: **Fat-soluble** (**A, D, E, and K**) and **Water-soluble** (**B-complex and Vitamin C**).
 
• **Water-soluble vitamins** are not stored in the body and must be consumed regularly through **diet**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sources of Vitamin B1:** Rich dietary sources include **whole grains**, **legumes** (beans and lentils), **nuts**, **seeds**, **pork**, and **yeast**.
 
• **Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA):** The daily requirement for **Thiamine** for an **adult male** is approximately **1.2 mg** and for an **adult female** is **1.1 mg**.
 
• **Wernicke-Korsakoff Syndrome:** This is another severe disorder related to **Thiamine deficiency**, often observed in individuals with **chronic alcoholism**, as alcohol interferes with **thiamine absorption** in the **intestines**.
 
• **Historical Context:** In **1897**, **Christiaan Eijkman** discovered that feeding **unpolished rice** instead of polished rice to chickens could prevent a disease similar to **Beri-beri**, which eventually led to the discovery of **vitamins**.

questions.question: Which Indian city is known as the “Silicon Valley of India” due to its thriving IT services sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengaluru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bengaluru** is widely recognized as the **Silicon Valley of India** because it is the nation's leading **Information Technology (IT)** exporter. This city, located in the state of **Karnataka**, serves as the hub for major software companies and tech startups. ***Hence, option D is correct.***
 
• The city began its transformation into a tech giant in the **1980s** when the **Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation (KEONICS)** established **Electronic City**. In **1985**, **Texas Instruments** became the first multinational corporation to set up a base in the city, paving the way for others.
 
• It hosts the headquarters of prominent Indian IT firms like **Infosys** and **Wipro**, as well as significant operations for global companies such as **Google**, **Microsoft**, **Amazon**, and **IBM**.
 
• The presence of prestigious educational and research institutions like the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)** and the **Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB)** provides a steady supply of skilled human resources, fueling the **innovation ecosystem**.
 
• **Bengaluru** accounts for nearly **33% to 35%** of India's total **IT exports**, making it a critical driver of the national economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hyderabad (Option A)**: Often referred to as **Cyberabad**, it is a major competitor to Bengaluru in the **IT** and **Biotechnology** sectors. It houses the **HITEC City** (Hyderabad Information Technology and Engineering Consultancy City) and major offices of **Microsoft** (its largest campus outside the US) and **Facebook**. However, it is not primarily known as the Silicon Valley of India. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Mumbai (Option B)**: Known as the **Financial Capital of India**, it is the home of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, **Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE)**, and **National Stock Exchange (NSE)**. While it has an IT presence through **SEEPZ** (Santacruz Electronic Export Processing Zone), its identity is rooted in **banking**, **finance**, and the **entertainment industry (Bollywood)**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Chennai (Option C)**: Known as the **Detroit of Asia** due to its massive **automobile industry**, hosting companies like **Hyundai**, **Ford**, and **Renault-Nissan**. It is also called the **Health Capital of India** due to its advanced medical tourism. While it has a strong IT corridor on **Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR)**, it is not the primary Silicon Valley. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• **Software Technology Parks of India (STPI)**: Established in **1991** under the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology**, this organization has played a vital role in promoting software exports from cities like Bengaluru by providing **infrastructure** and **statutory services**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographic Advantage**: Bengaluru is situated on the **Deccan Plateau** at an elevation of over **900 meters** above sea level, providing a **pleasant climate** throughout the year, which historically attracted **British** colonists and later tech professionals.
 
• **Public Sector Heritage**: Before the IT boom, the city was a center for **heavy industries** and **aerospace**. It is home to the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**, and **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**.
 
• **Startup Culture**: As of the **2020s**, Bengaluru is frequently ranked among the top **global startup hubs**, often appearing alongside cities like **San Francisco** and **London** in terms of **venture capital** investment and **unicorn** (startups valued over **$1 billion**) creation.
 
• **Infrastructure**: Key tech parks such as **Manyata Tech Park**, **Bagmane Tech Park**, and **Whitefield** are central to the city's status as a **global technology node**.

questions.question: A tourist covers his 120 km journey in three stages. In the first stage, he travels at a speed of x km/hr. In the second stage, he increases his speed by 50%. In the third stage, he reduces his second-stage speed by 20%. He spends equal time on all the 3 stages, and his average speed for the entire journey is 48 km/hr. Find the value of x correct to one decimal place.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equal time ⇒ Average speed = (v1 + v2 + v3) ÷ 3

v1 = x, v2 = 1.5x, v3 = 0.8 × 1.5x = 1.2x

Average = (x + 1.5x + 1.2x)/3 = 3.7x/3

⇒ 3.7x/3 = 48

⇒ x = 48 × 3 / 3.7 = 144/3.7 ≈ 38.9

**∴ Answer = 38.9 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 120 km, equal time in 3 stages, average speed = 48 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average speed (equal time) = (v1 + v2 + v3) ÷ 3

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let speed in first stage = x

⇒ Second stage speed = x + 50% of x = 1.5x

⇒ Third stage speed = 1.5x − 20% of 1.5x = 1.2x

⇒ Average speed = (x + 1.5x + 1.2x) ÷ 3

⇒ 48 = (3.7x) ÷ 3

⇒ 144 = 3.7x

⇒ x = 144 ÷ 3.7

⇒ x ≈ 38.9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 38.9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Time)

If time is same, average speed = arithmetic mean of speeds

Percentage Change

Increase: multiply by (1 + p/100), Decrease: multiply by (1 − p/100)

Successive Change

Apply changes step-by-step (not directly combined unless simplified)

Key Insight

Equal time problems avoid distance complexity by using average of speeds

questions.question: In 2025, Bagram Air Base, the largest air base mentioned in the news after U.S. President Donald Trump’s bid to retake it, is located in which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Afghanistan**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bagram Air Base** is the largest airfield in **Afghanistan**, located in the **Parwan Province**, approximately **11 kilometers** southeast of **Charikar** and **40 kilometers** north of the capital city, **Kabul**.
 
• The base served as the epicenter of the **United States** military operations and **NATO**’s **Resolute Support Mission** during the war in **Afghanistan** from **2001** to **2021**.
 
• In **July 2021**, **U.S. forces** vacated the base in a middle-of-the-night departure, which marked a symbolic end to the **20-year** military presence; shortly after, in **August 2021**, the **Taliban** took full control of the facility.
 
• The base came back into the spotlight in **2024** and **2025** following statements by **Donald Trump** during his presidential campaign, where he argued that the **U.S.** should have kept the base not for **Afghanistan** itself, but because of its strategic proximity to **China’s** nuclear testing sites.
 
• The airfield has historically been a critical logistical hub, featuring **two massive runways** capable of accommodating the world's largest military aircraft, such as the **C-5 Galaxy** and **Boeing C-17 Globemaster III**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Background**: The base was originally built by the **Soviet Union** in the **1950s** during the **Cold War** and was a major base of operations for the **Soviet Army** during the **Soviet-Afghan War** (**1979–1989**).
 
• **Strategic Geography**: It is situated at an elevation of about **1,492 meters** (4,895 feet) above sea level in the **Shamali Plain**, surrounded by the peaks of the **Hindu Kush** mountains, making it a natural fortress for aerial surveillance and defense.

⇒ √(756 + 28) = √784 = 28

⇒ √(x³ − 1/x³ + 28) = √(756 + 28)

questions.question: Which Article deals with the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 131**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 131** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the **Original Jurisdiction** of the **Supreme Court**. It empowers the court to hear disputes at the first instance, rather than through an appeal.
 
• This jurisdiction is **exclusive**, meaning no other court in India (including High Courts) can adjudicate on matters involving federal disputes. This is a crucial feature of the **Federal Structure** of the Indian polity.
 
• The scope of **Article 131** covers disputes between:
 
 
• The **Government of India** (Centre) and one or more **States**.
 
• The **Government of India** and any **State or States** on one side and one or more other **States** on the other.
 
• Two or more **States** against each other.
 
 
 
• For a dispute to be maintainable under **Article 131**, it must involve a question of **law or fact** on which the existence or extent of a **legal right** depends. ***Hence, the statement regarding Article 131 being the original jurisdiction is correct.***
 
• The **Supreme Court** acts as an **arbiter** in these cases to maintain the balance of power between the union and the units of the federation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 124:**

 
 
• It provides for the **establishment and constitution** of the **Supreme Court of India**.
 
• It states that there shall be a **Supreme Court** consisting of a **Chief Justice of India** and other judges. The current sanctioned strength is **34** judges (including the CJI).
 
• It outlines the **qualifications**, **appointment**, and **removal process** (impeachment) of judges. ***Hence, the statement regarding Article 124 dealing with original jurisdiction is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Article 32:**
 
 
• Known as the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**, it allows citizens to move the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights**.
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** called this article the **"Heart and Soul of the Constitution."**
 
• Under this article, the court can issue **writs** such as **Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**, **Prohibition**, **Certiorari**, and **Quo-Warranto**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Article 32 being the federal original jurisdiction is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Article 141:**
 
 
• It states that the **law declared** by the **Supreme Court** shall be **binding on all courts** within the territory of **India**.
 
• This ensures **uniformity** and **certainty** in the legal system across the **country**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Article 141 dealing with original jurisdiction is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exclusions from Article 131:**

 
 
• The **Original Jurisdiction** does not extend to disputes arising out of any **pre-Constitution treaty**, agreement, covenant, or engagement which is still in force.
 
• Disputes related to **Inter-State Water Disputes** are excluded under **Article 262** of the Constitution, for which **Tribunals** are typically established.
 
• Matters referred to the **Finance Commission** under **Article 280** are also outside the purview of **Article 131**.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• Under **Article 143**, the **President of India** can seek the **opinion** of the **Supreme Court** on questions of law or fact of **public importance**.
 
 
 
• **Appellate Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• The **Supreme Court** is the **highest court of appeal** in the **country**. It hears appeals against the judgments of **High Courts** under **Articles 132, 133, and 134**.

questions.question: What term describes a situation in which a person is employed but not in the desired capacity, in terms of compensation, hours, or skill level?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Underemployment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Underemployment** is a measure of employment and labor utilization in the economy that looks at how well the labor force is being used in terms of **skills, experience, and availability to work**.
 
• It occurs when a person is technically **employed** but is working in a capacity that is lower than their **educational qualifications**, **professional experience**, or **desired number of hours**. *Hence, the statement provided in the question accurately describes Underemployment, making it the correct option.*
 
• There are two main types of underemployment: **Visible Underemployment**, where employees work fewer hours than is considered normal or desired in their field, and **Invisible Underemployment**, where employees work in jobs that do not utilize their **specialized skills**.
 
• In the context of **India**, underemployment is a significant challenge as many highly educated individuals (engineers, post-graduates) are often forced to take up **low-skilled jobs** in the **informal sector** due to a lack of suitable opportunities.
 
• The **International Labour Organization (ILO)** notes that underemployment leads to **economic inefficiency** because the potential productivity of the workforce is not being fully realized, which can hinder a nation’s **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Part-time employment:**

 
 
• This refers to a form of employment that carries **fewer hours** per week than a **full-time** job (usually less than **30-35 hours**).
 
• While it can be **voluntary** (for students or parents), it becomes a form of underemployment when it is **involuntary**, meaning the worker wants full-time work but cannot find it. *Hence, this option is only a subset of the broader definition provided.*
 
 
 
• **Involuntary employment:**
 
 
• This term is less common than **Involuntary Unemployment**, which refers to a situation where people are willing to work at the **prevailing wage rate** but cannot find a job.
 
• If used to describe a person currently working, it implies they have no choice but to work in their current role to survive, even if the **conditions** are poor. *Hence, it does not specifically focus on the capacity of skills or hours like underemployment does.*
 
 
 
• **Low wage employment:**
 
 
• This refers specifically to jobs that pay **wages** at or near the **poverty line** or below the **minimum wage** set by the **government**.
 
• While underemployed people often earn low wages, low wage employment is strictly a **monetary metric** and does not necessarily account for the **skill mismatch** or **underutilization of time**. *Hence, this option focuses only on compensation, not capacity.*
 
 
 
• **Disguised Unemployment:**
 
 
• Common in the **Agricultural sector** in **India**, this is a form of underemployment where more people are working than are actually needed.
 
• If some people are removed, the **total production** remains the same, meaning their **marginal productivity** is **zero**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statistical Monitoring:** In **India**, the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** conducts the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** to estimate indicators of **labor force participation**, **employment**, and **unemployment** across the country.
 
• **Economic Causes:** Underemployment often increases during an **economic recession** or when there is a significant **structural shift** in the economy (e.g., transition from **manufacturing** to **services**) that leaves certain skill sets **obsolete**.
 
• **Impact on Youth:** Data suggests that **youth underemployment** is a rising concern globally, leading to **lower lifetime earnings** and **reduced social mobility** as young workers fail to gain relevant experience during their **prime working years**.
 
• **Brain Drain:** Persistent underemployment in a **country** can lead to **human capital flight** or **Brain Drain**, where skilled professionals migrate to other countries in search of jobs that match their **competencies**.

questions.question: Harshavardhana’s biography Harshacharita was composed in Sanskrit by which of the following court poets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banabhatta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banabhatta** was the **Asthana Kavi** (court poet) of the **Emperor Harshavardhana**, who ruled **North India** from **606 to 647 CE**. He is one of the most celebrated prose writers in the history of **Sanskrit literature**.
 
• He composed the **Harshacharita** (The Deeds of Harsha), which is considered the first **historical biography** written in the **Sanskrit language**. The text provides a detailed account of **Harsha's** ancestry, his rise to the throne, and the socio-political conditions of the **7th century**.
 
• Apart from the biography, **Banabhatta** is also the author of **Kadambari**, which is one of the world's earliest and most famous **romance novels** written in **Sanskrit**. Unfortunately, he passed away before completing it, and his son **Bhushanabhatta** finished the work.
 
• The **Harshacharita** consists of **eight chapters** called **Uchchhavasas**. The first two chapters are **autobiographical**, where the author describes his own lineage, while the remaining chapters focus on the **Vardhana Dynasty** and the exploits of **King Harsha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harshavardhana**:

 
 
• He belonged to the **Pushyabhuti dynasty** (also known as the **Vardhana dynasty**). After the death of his brother **Rajyavardhana**, he ascended the throne at the **age of 16** in **606 AD**.
 
• He shifted his capital from **Thanesar** to **Kannauj** (modern-day **Uttar Pradesh**) to better manage his expanding empire.
 
• He was a great patron of **Buddhism** and learning. The famous **Chinese traveler Xuanzang** (Hiuen Tsang) visited India during his reign and stayed in his court for several years, providing a vivid description of the **administration** and **society**.
 
• **Harsha** himself was a renowned scholar and authored three famous **Sanskrit plays**: **Ratnavali**, **Priyadarshika**, and **Nagananda**.
 
 
 
• **Ravikirti**:
 
 
• He was the court poet of the **Chalukya King Pulakeshin II**. He is famous for composing the **Aihole Inscription** in **634 AD**.
 
• The inscription is a significant **historical source** as it mentions the defeat of **Harshavardhana** by **Pulakeshin II** on the banks of the **Narmada River**.
 
 
 
• **Vishnu Sharma**:
 
 
• He is the legendary author of the **Panchatantra**, one of the most translated non-religious books in history.
 
• The **Panchatantra** is a collection of **interwoven animal fables** written in **Sanskrit**, intended to teach **niti** (political science and wise conduct) to young princes. It likely dates back to the **Gupta period** (around **300 CE**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context**: The era of **Harshavardhana** marked the transition from the **Ancient period** to the **Early Medieval period** in India. His empire covered much of **North and Northwestern India**, extending to the **Narmada** in the south and **Ganjam** in the east.
 
• **Religious Tolerance**: Although initially a worshiper of **Shiva**, **Harsha** became a great supporter of **Mahayana Buddhism**. He organized the **Kannauj Assembly** in **643 AD** to honor **Xuanzang** and propagate **Buddhist doctrines**.
 
• **Literary Style**: **Banabhatta's** style is known as **Panchali-riti**, characterized by long **compounds**, elaborate **descriptions**, and the frequent use of **figures of speech** like metaphors and puns. His work provides essential data regarding the **military organization**, **feudal structure**, and **religious festivals** (like the **Kumbh Mela** at **Prayag**) of that time.

questions.question: Who is widely regarded as the ‘Father of Computers’ for designing the first mechanical computing device?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charles Babbage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charles Babbage**, an English mathematician and inventor, is widely recognized as the **"Father of the Computer"** for his pioneering work in conceptualizing and designing the first mechanical computers.
 
• In **1822**, Babbage proposed and began developing the **Difference Engine**, a mechanical calculator designed to tabulate polynomial functions and calculate mathematical tables automatically, reducing human error.
 
• His most ambitious project, the **Analytical Engine**, designed around **1837**, is considered the first design for a **general-purpose computer**. It incorporated key concepts of modern computing, such as an **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)**, control flow in the form of **conditional branching** and **loops**, and **integrated memory**.
 
• The **Analytical Engine** used **punched cards** (inspired by the **Jacquard loom**) for input, which allowed it to be programmed to perform various mathematical operations rather than being fixed to a single task.
 
• Although Babbage was never able to complete a full-scale working version of his machines during his lifetime due to funding issues and technical limitations of the **19th century**, his detailed drawings and logic laid the essential groundwork for the **digital revolution** in the **20th century**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Blaise Pascal:**

 
 
• In **1642**, at the age of 19, the French mathematician **Blaise Pascal** invented the **Pascaline**.
 
• The **Pascaline** was the first **mechanical calculator** capable of performing addition and subtraction directly. It utilized a series of **gears and wheels** and was primarily used by his father, a tax collector, to ease complex calculations.
 
 
 
• **Alan Turing:**
 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **"Father of Modern Computing"** and **"Father of Artificial Intelligence"**, **Alan Turing** was a British polymath.
 
• He formulated the concept of the **Turing Machine** in **1936**, which provided the formal logic for how a computer processes symbols. During **World War II**, his work at **Bletchley Park** was instrumental in cracking the German **Enigma code**.
 
 
 
• **John von Neumann:**
 
 
• A Hungarian-American mathematician who proposed the **von Neumann architecture** in **1945**.
 
• This architecture describes a **stored-program computer** where both instruction data and program data are stored in the same **random-access memory (RAM)**. This remains the fundamental design for nearly all modern computers today.
 
 
 
• **Ada Lovelace:**
 
 
• An English mathematician known for her work on Babbage's **Analytical Engine**.
 
• She is widely regarded as the world's **first computer programmer** because she wrote an algorithm intended to be processed by a machine, recognizing that the computer had applications beyond mere calculation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Computing:** The transition from **mechanical devices** like the **Abacus** and **Pascaline** to **electromechanical** and eventually **electronic digital computers** like **ENIAC** (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer) was spurred by the logical foundations set by **Babbage**.
 
• **Difference Engine No. 2:** Between **1989 and 1991**, the **Science Museum in London** successfully built a working version of Babbage's **Difference Engine No. 2** using his original plans, proving that his designs were technically sound and accurate to within **31 decimal places**.
 
• **Technical Components:** Babbage's designs identified four essential components found in modern systems: the **"Store"** (Memory), the **"Mill"** (Processor), the **"Reader"** (Input), and the **"Printer"** (Output).

• **IPC (Instructions Per Cycle)** is a performance metric that represents the average number of **machine instructions** a **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** can execute in a single **clock cycle**. It serves as a primary measure of a **processor's microarchitecture** efficiency. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• The **IPC** of a **CPU** is not a fixed number; it varies based on the type of **software code** being run and the **complexity** of the instructions. Tasks involving simple **integer math** typically yield a higher **IPC** than complex **floating-point** operations.
 
• Modern **high-performance CPUs** utilize **superscalar architecture**, which allows them to execute more than one instruction per cycle by having multiple **execution units** (like **ALUs**) working in parallel.
 
• Factors that influence **IPC** include the **size of the cache** (L1, L2, and L3), the efficiency of the **branch predictor**, and the **pipeline depth**. A deeper **pipeline** may allow for higher **clock speeds** but can sometimes lower the **IPC** due to the penalty of **branch mispredictions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Clock Speed**: Measured in **Gigahertz (GHz)** or **Megahertz (MHz)**, it indicates the number of **pulses** or **cycles** generated by an oscillator per second. While it tells us how fast the **CPU** "ticks," it does not reveal how much work is done during each tick. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Bus Speed**: This refers to the frequency at which the **Front Side Bus (FSB)** or modern interconnects (like **Intel's QPI** or **AMD's Infinity Fabric**) communicate between the **CPU** and the **Northbridge** or **System Memory (RAM)**. It determines the **bandwidth** available for data transfer rather than **instruction execution**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Core Count**: This is the number of independent **processing cores** integrated into a single **computing component**. While having more **cores** allows a **computer** to handle more **threads** simultaneously (parallelism), it is an aggregate measure of capacity rather than a per-cycle efficiency metric. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• **The Performance Formula**: The overall **speed** of a **CPU** is determined by the product of **Clock Speed** and **IPC**. This explains why a modern **3.0 GHz** processor can outperform an older **4.0 GHz** processor from a previous **decade**; the newer **architecture** has a much higher **IPC**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context**: In the **late 1990s** and **early 2000s**, manufacturers primarily focused on **clock speed** (the **Megahertz myth**). However, as **power consumption** and **heat dissipation** became issues, companies like **Intel** and **AMD** shifted focus toward improving **IPC** to gain performance without increasing **power**.
 
• **MIPS vs IPC**: **MIPS (Millions of Instructions Per Second)** is another way to measure **CPU** speed, but it is considered less reliable than **IPC** because it does not account for the **complexity** of different instruction sets (like **RISC** vs **CISC**).
 
• **Bottlenecks**: Even if a **CPU** has a high theoretical **IPC**, it can be limited by **memory latency**. If the **data** is not in the **L1 cache**, the **CPU** must wait hundreds of **cycles** to fetch it from **RAM**, causing the effective **IPC** to drop.

questions.question: Which event best signalled the decline of Portuguese power in India and the emergence of British and Dutch influence?

options.text: Establishment of Madras by the English (1639)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anglo-Persian capture of Hormuz (1622)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Anglo-Persian capture of Hormuz** in **1622** was a decisive military campaign where the **English East India Company** joined forces with the **Safavid Empire** of **Persia** (under **Shah Abbas I**) to expel the **Portuguese** from the **Island of Hormuz**. This event was the primary signal of the decline of **Portuguese** naval supremacy in the **Indian Ocean**. ***Hence, Option C is the correct answer.***
 
• The **Battle of Plassey** took place in **1757** between the **British East India Company** and the **Nawab of Bengal** (supported by the **French**). While it established **British** political hegemony in **India**, it occurred over a century after the **Portuguese** power had already waned. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• The **Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle** was signed in **1748** to end the **War of the Austrian Succession**. In the context of **India**, it concluded the **First Carnatic War** between the **English** and the **French**, returning **Madras** to the **British**. It did not directly involve the decline of the **Portuguese**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• The **Establishment of Madras** by the **English** occurred in **1639** when **Francis Day** obtained a grant from the **Raja of Chandragiri**. While it represented **British** growth, the strategic naval defeat at **Hormuz** earlier in **1622** was the specific turning point that broke the **Portuguese** commercial monopoly. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***
 
• The loss of **Hormuz** meant the **Portuguese** lost control of the **Persian Gulf**, which was a vital "choke point" for trade. This allowed the **Dutch East India Company (VOC)** and the **English** to aggressively expand their influence in the spice and textile trades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Portuguese Arrival and Rule:** The **Portuguese** were the first **Europeans** to reach **India** via the sea route when **Vasco da Gama** arrived at **Calicut** in **1498**. They established their headquarters at **Goa** in **1510** under **Alfonso de Albuquerque**. Their power was maintained through the **Cartaz System**, a naval license or pass issued to merchant ships to control sea trade.
 
• **The Rise of the Dutch (VOC):** The **United East India Company of the Netherlands** was formed in **1602**. The **Dutch** focused on the **East Indies** (modern-day **Indonesia**) but also established factories in **India** at **Masulipatnam** (**1605**), **Pulicat** (**1610**), and **Surat** (**1616**). Their superior naval technology and financial backing posed a direct threat to **Portuguese** strongholds.
 
• **English East India Company Growth:** Following the **Battle of Swally** in **1612**, where **Captain Best** defeated a **Portuguese** fleet, the **English** gained the favor of the **Mughal Emperor Jahangir**. This led to the establishment of their first permanent factory at **Surat** in **1613**.
 
• **Strategic Locations:** By the mid-**17th century**, the **Portuguese** were restricted to small enclaves like **Goa**, **Daman**, and **Diu**, while the **British** developed the three major presidencies of **Bombay**, **Madras**, and **Calcutta**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Battle of Swally (1612):** This was a small naval engagement off the coast of **Surat**. Though minor, it is historically significant because it convinced **Mughal** authorities that the **English** could provide a naval counter-balance to the **Portuguese**.
 
• **Religious Policy:** One major reason for the decline of **Portuguese** influence was their aggressive **proselytization** and **religious intolerance**, which alienated both **Hindu** and **Muslim** rulers in **India**, unlike the initially purely commercial approach of the **English** and **Dutch**.
 
• **The Dutch-Portuguese War:** A global conflict spanning the **17th century** where the **Dutch** systematically seized **Portuguese** colonies in **Ceylon (Sri Lanka)**, **Malacca**, and the **Malabar Coast** (notably **Cochin** in **1663**).

questions.question: What is the inflation target set by the Government of India under the Monetary Policy Committee framework until April 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4% with a tolerance of ±2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India**, in consultation with the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, has fixed the inflation target at **4%** with a tolerance band of **+/- 2%**. This means the target range is effectively **2% to 6%**.
 
• This specific target was originally set for the period of **August 5, 2016**, to **March 31, 2021**, and was subsequently retained for the next **five-year period** from **April 1, 2021**, to **March 31, 2026**.
 
• The target is based on the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**, specifically the **CPI-Combined** index, which measures the average change in prices paid by consumers for a basket of goods and services.
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** is statutory and institutionalized under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of **economic growth**.
 
• If the **inflation** remains above **6%** or below **2%** for **3 consecutive quarters**, it is considered a failure of the monetary policy framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Legal Framework:** The framework for **Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT)** was established following an amendment to the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, through the **Finance Act, 2016**. This provided a **statutory basis** for the conduct of monetary policy in **India**.
 
• **Committee Composition:** The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** consists of **6 members**. This includes **3 members** from the **Reserve Bank of India** (including the **Governor** and **Deputy Governor**) and **3 external members** appointed by the **Central Government** based on the recommendations of a **search-cum-selection committee**.
 
• **Urjit Patel Committee:** The shift towards inflation targeting was primarily based on the recommendations of the **Urjit Patel Committee report** submitted in **January 2014**, which suggested that **CPI** should be the anchor of monetary policy.
 
• **Operational Instrument:** The **Policy Repo Rate** is the main instrument used by the **MPC** to keep the **inflation** within the target band. Changes in the **repo rate** influence the overall interest rates in the **economy**.
 
• **Accountability:** Under **Section 45ZN** of the **RBI Act**, if the **RBI** fails to meet the inflation target, it must set out in a report to the **Central Government** the reasons for the failure and the **remedial actions** proposed to be taken, along with an **estimated time period** within which the target shall be achieved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Meeting Frequency:** The **MPC** is required to meet at least **four times** a **year**. The decisions are made by a **majority vote**, and the **Governor** of the **RBI** has a **casting vote** in the event of a tie.
 
• **Transparency:** The **RBI** is mandated to publish a **Monetary Policy Report** every **six months**, explaining the sources of **inflation** and the forecasts for the next **6 to 18 months**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** Maintaining **price stability** (low and stable inflation) is crucial for **macroeconomic stability**, as it helps in protecting the purchasing power of the **rupee** and encourages **investment** and **savings** within the **country**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Prior to the **2016** amendment, **India** followed a "multiple indicator approach," but the high **inflation** levels during **2009-2013** necessitated a move toward a more focused **nominal anchor**.

questions.question: Momentum of an object is defined as the product of its mass and velocity, hence what are its SI units?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kg m s–¹**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Momentum** is a fundamental concept in physics, defined as the quantity of motion an object possesses. It is mathematically expressed as the product of an object's **mass** and its **velocity** (**p = m × v**).
 
• To determine the **SI unit** of momentum, we analyze the basic units of the physical quantities involved. The **SI unit** for **mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**, and the **SI unit** for **velocity** is **meters per second (m/s or m s–¹)**.
 
• By multiplying these base units (**kg** and **m s–¹**), we derive the **SI unit** for momentum as **kg m s–¹**. *Hence, option D is correct.*
 
• **Momentum** is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**. The direction of the momentum vector is always the same as the direction of the **velocity** of the object.
 
• The unit **kg m s–²** represents the **Newton (N)**, which is the **SI unit** of **Force**, not momentum. *Hence, statement/option B is incorrect.*
 
• The unit **g m s–¹** is a metric unit but not the standard **International System of Units (SI)** unit, as the **SI** system requires mass to be in **kilograms**. *Hence, statement/option A is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:** This law states that the **force** applied to an object is equal to the rate of change of its **momentum** (**F = dp/dt**). This establishes a direct relationship between **force**, **mass**, and **acceleration**.
 
• **Law of Conservation of Momentum:** In the absence of an external **force**, the total **momentum** of a closed system remains **constant**. This principle is vital in analyzing **collisions** and **explosions**, where the initial momentum equals the final momentum.
 
• **Impulse:** **Impulse** is defined as the change in **momentum** of an object when a **force** acts upon it for an interval of **time**. The **SI unit** for impulse is the **Newton-second (N s)**, which is dimensionally equivalent to **kg m s–¹**.
 
• **Factors Affecting Momentum:**
 
 
• **Mass:** If two objects travel at the same **velocity**, the one with the higher **mass** will have greater **momentum**. For example, a **truck** has more momentum than a **bicycle** moving at the same speed.
 
• **Velocity:** If two objects have the same **mass**, the one with the higher **velocity** will have more **momentum**. A **bullet**, despite its small **mass**, has immense **momentum** due to its extremely high **velocity**.
 
 
 
• **Applications:** The concept of **momentum** is used in designing **safety features** in vehicles, such as **airbags** and **crumple zones**, which aim to increase the **time** over which the **momentum** changes during a crash, thereby reducing the **impact force**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **CGS unit** of **momentum** is **g cm s–¹** (gram-centimeter per second).
 
• In **Relativistic Mechanics**, the formula for **momentum** changes as the **velocity** approaches the **speed of light (c)**, incorporating the **Lorentz factor**.
 
• The **dimensions** of **momentum** are **[M L T–¹]**.
 
• An object at rest has a **velocity** of **zero**, and therefore its **momentum** is also **zero**, regardless of its **mass**.

questions.question: According to the Gandhian principles incorporated in the Directive Principles of State Policy, the State shall endeavor to promote:

options.text: Cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 43** of the **Constitution of India** explicitly states that the **State** shall endeavor to promote **cottage industries** on an **individual or cooperative basis** in **rural areas**. This is a direct reflection of the **Gandhian ideology** of rural self-sufficiency and economic decentralization. Hence, the statement regarding cottage industries is correct.
 
• The **Gandhian principles** within the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** represent the program of reconstruction enunciated by **Mahatma Gandhi** during the national movement. These principles aim to empower the rural population and promote **local self-government**.
 
• Promotion of **corporate farming** or large-scale **industrialization in urban areas** does not align with the **Gandhian** focus on the "village-level economy." Gandhi believed that India's soul lives in its **villages**, and thus economic activities should be centered around **village-level production**. Hence, options A and B are incorrect.
 
• The emphasis on **cooperative basis** ensures that the workers or artisans have collective ownership and bargaining power, preventing exploitation by middlemen or large corporations. This aligns with the **Gandhian concept of Trusteeship** and **Swadeshi**.
 
• The **State** is expected to provide **financial assistance**, technical training, and **marketing support** to these small-scale rural units to ensure they can compete and provide a sustainable **livelihood** to the rural masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of DPSP:** The **Directive Principles of State Policy**, contained in **Part IV** (**Articles 36 to 51**), are generally classified into three categories: **Socialistic Principles**, **Gandhian Principles**, and **Liberal-Intellectual Principles**.
 
• **Other Gandhian Principles in DPSP:**
 
 
• **Article 40:** To organize **village panchayats** and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of **self-government**.
 
• **Article 43B:** To promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of **co-operative societies** (Added by the **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011**).
 
• **Article 46:** To promote the **educational and economic interests** of **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**, **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**, and other **weaker sections** of the society.
 
• **Article 47:** To prohibit the consumption of **intoxicating drinks** and **drugs** which are injurious to health.
 
• **Article 48:** To prohibit the **slaughter of cows**, calves, and other milch and draught cattle and to improve their breeds.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Cottage Industries:** These industries are characterized by **low capital investment**, use of **local raw materials**, and employment of **family labor**. They are vital for **rural development** in a country like **India** where a large portion of the population resides in **villages**.
 
• **Nature of DPSP:** These principles are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation (**Article 37**). However, they are fundamental in the **governance** of the country, and it is the duty of the **State** to apply these principles in making laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Source of DPSP:** The concept of **Directive Principles of State Policy** was borrowed from the **Irish Constitution** of **1937**, which had copied it from the **Spanish Constitution**.
 
• **Objective:** The primary goal of these directives is to establish a **Welfare State** in **India** and to ensure **Social and Economic Democracy**, supplementing the **Political Democracy** established by the **Fundamental Rights**.
 
• **Constitutional Status:** In the **Minerva Mills case (1980)**, the **Supreme Court** held that the Indian Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the **balance** between the **Fundamental Rights** and the **Directive Principles**.
 
• **Implementation:** Various government schemes like the **Kadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)**, established in **1956**, were created to fulfill the mandate of **Article 43** and promote rural **entrepreneurship**.

questions.question: Which term is used to describe the conflict between the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, and Rashtrakutas over the control of northern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tripartite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Tripartite Struggle** is used to describe the prolonged conflict between the three major powers of the early medieval period: the **Gurjara-Pratiharas**, the **Palas**, and the **Rashtrakutas**.
 
• The primary cause of this conflict was the desire to control **Kannauj**, a city in **Northern India** that served as a symbol of imperial sovereignty since the reign of **Harsha Vardhana**.
 
• This struggle for supremacy lasted for nearly **two centuries**, beginning in the late **8th century AD** and continuing into the **10th century AD**.
 
• Control over **Kannauj** meant control over the fertile and resource-rich **Gangetic Valley**, providing significant economic and strategic advantages to the ruling dynasty.
 
• While different dynasties gained temporary control over the city at various times, the continuous warfare eventually exhausted the resources of all **three empires**, leading to their eventual disintegration.

questions.question: Under the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016, who has the exclusive power to make laws on GST, where the supply of goods or services takes place in the course of interstate trade or commerce?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016**, introduced the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** regime in India, which officially came into force on **1 July 2017**.
 
• Under **Article 246A(2)** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **Parliament** has been granted the **exclusive power** to make laws with respect to **goods and services tax** where the supply of goods, or of services, or both, takes place in the course of **inter-state trade or commerce**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Parliament's exclusive power over interstate trade is correct.***
 
• While **Article 246A(1)** confers concurrent power upon both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** to make laws with respect to **GST** levied by the **Union** or by such **State**, this concurrent power is limited to **intra-state** transactions.
 
• The **Parliament** exercised this exclusive power by enacting the **Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2017**, to regulate the tax on the movement of goods and services from one state to another.
 
• The **President of India** does not have the legislative power to make laws on **GST** but is responsible for constituting the **GST Council** under **Article 279A**. ***Hence, the option involving the President is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 269A:** This article specifies that **GST** on supplies in the course of **inter-state trade or commerce** shall be levied and collected by the **Government of India**. This tax is then apportioned between the **Union** and the **States** based on the recommendations of the **GST Council**.
 
• **The GST Council:** Established under **Article 279A**, the council is a **constitutional body** chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**. It includes the **Union Minister of State** in charge of Revenue or Finance and the **Finance Ministers** of all states. It makes recommendations on tax rates, exemptions, and threshold limits.
 
• **NITI Aayog:** The **National Institution for Transforming India** is a policy think tank of the **Government of India** established on **1 January 2015**. It does not possess legislative powers to enact tax laws like **GST**. ***Hence, the option involving NITI Aayog is incorrect.***
 
• **State Legislatures:** Under the **101st Amendment**, **State Legislatures** have the power to make laws for **GST** imposed by the State (**SGST**) for transactions within the state boundaries, but they lack the authority to legislate on **inter-state** supplies. ***Hence, the option involving State Legislatures as having exclusive power for interstate trade is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dual GST Model:** India adopted a **dual GST model** (similar to **Canada**), meaning that **GST** is administered by both the **Union** and the **State governments**.
 
• **Taxes Subsumed:** The **GST** replaced several **indirect taxes**, including **Central Excise Duty**, **Service Tax**, **Additional Customs Duty**, **State VAT**, **Entry Tax**, and **Luxury Tax**.
 
• **Destination-Based Tax:** Unlike the previous **origin-based** taxation system, **GST** is a **consumption-based** or **destination-based tax**, meaning the revenue accrues to the state where the goods or services are finally consumed.
 
• **Compensation to States:** To ease the transition, the **Parliament** enacted the **GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017**, guaranteeing compensation to states for any **revenue loss** for a period of **5 years** (initially until **June 2022**).

questions.question: Thermal pollution primarily results from which action related to industrial processes?

options.text: Use of water as a coolant

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Use of water as a coolant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thermal pollution** is defined as the sudden increase or decrease in the temperature of a **natural body of water**, such as an ocean, lake, river, or pond, by human influence.
 
• In industrial processes, **water is widely used as a coolant** to remove excess heat from machinery and power-generating equipment. This is most common in **thermal power plants**, **nuclear reactors**, and **oil refineries**.
 
• Once the water has absorbed the heat, it is often discharged back into the environment at a **significantly higher temperature** than the ambient water temperature. ***Hence, the statement regarding the use of water as a coolant is correct.***
 
• The primary biological impact is the **reduction of dissolved oxygen (DO)**. As water temperature rises, its ability to hold oxygen decreases, which can lead to the **suffocation of fish** and other aquatic aerobic organisms.
 
• Sudden changes in temperature can cause **thermal shock**, leading to the mass mortality of **vulnerable aquatic species** that cannot adapt quickly to the new environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Addition of Detergents:** This primarily leads to **chemical water pollution**. Detergents often contain **phosphates**, which cause **eutrophication**—a process where excess nutrients lead to **algal blooms** that deplete oxygen. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect regarding thermal pollution.***
 
• **Release of Heavy Metals:** Industrial waste containing **mercury, lead, cadmium, and arsenic** leads to toxic pollution. These substances cause **bioaccumulation** in the food chain, resulting in diseases like **Minamata disease** (mercury) or **Itai-itai disease** (cadmium). ***Hence, this statement is incorrect regarding thermal pollution.***
 
• **Suspended Solid Accumulation:** This refers to **physical pollution**. High concentrations of suspended solids increase the **turbidity** of water, blocking **sunlight** and hindering the **photosynthesis** process of aquatic plants. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect regarding thermal pollution.***
 
• **Metabolic Impact:** Increased temperatures increase the **metabolic rate** of aquatic organisms, causing them to consume more food in a shorter time than if their environment were at a natural temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Framework:** In India, the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**, provides the legal framework to prevent and control water pollution, including **industrial thermal discharge**.
 
• **Mitigation Strategies:** Industries use **cooling towers**, **cooling ponds**, or **artificial lakes** to dissipate heat into the atmosphere through **evaporation or radiation** before the water is safely returned to natural bodies.
 
• **Nuclear Power Plants:** These facilities are major contributors to thermal pollution because they require **vast quantities of water** to cool their reactors. For example, plants located near **coastal areas** often discharge warm water directly into the **ocean**, affecting **coral reefs** and **marine biodiversity**.
 
• **Environmental Standards:** The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** sets specific **temperature limits** for industrial effluents to ensure that the temperature of the receiving water body does not rise by more than **5 degrees Celsius** above the ambient level.

questions.question:
Find the solution of the following system of linear equations:

x + 4y + 2z = 12

2x − y + z = 3

x + y − z = 0
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From (3): x + y − z = 0 ⇒ x = z − y

Substitute in (2): 2(z − y) − y + z = 3 ⇒ 3z − 3y = 3 ⇒ z − y = 1

⇒ x = 1

Use (1): 1 + 4y + 2(y + 1) = 12 ⇒ 6y + 3 = 12 ⇒ y = 3/2

⇒ z = y + 1 = 5/2

**∴ Answer: x = 1, y = 3/2, z = 5/2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + 4y + 2z = 12

2x − y + z = 3

x + y − z = 0

**Formula used:**

Elimination method

**Calculation:**

⇒ From (3): x = z − y

⇒ Substitute in (2): 2(z − y) − y + z = 3

⇒ 2z − 2y − y + z = 3

⇒ 3z − 3y = 3 ⇒ z − y = 1

⇒ ⇒ z = y + 1

⇒ Then x = z − y = 1

⇒ Substitute in (1): 1 + 4y + 2(y + 1) = 12

⇒ 1 + 4y + 2y + 2 = 12

⇒ 6y + 3 = 12

⇒ 6y = 9 ⇒ y = 3/2

⇒ z = y + 1 = 5/2

**∴ The correct answer is x = 1, y = 3/2, z = 5/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Elimination Method

Eliminate one variable to reduce equations step-by-step.

Express one variable in terms of others and substitute.

System has unique solution when equations intersect at one point.

Substitute values back to verify correctness.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a document related to Good Governance?

__
 
• **Good Governance** refers to the process of decision-making and the process by which decisions are implemented (or not implemented). It is characterized by **accountability, transparency, responsiveness, equity and inclusiveness, effectiveness and efficiency, and the rule of law.**
 
• **Citizen Charter**: It is a document that represents a systematic effort to focus on the commitment of the **Organisation **towards its Citizens in respect of **Standard of Services, Information, Choice and Consultation, Non-discrimination and Accessibility, Grievance Redress, Courtesy, and Value for Money**. It was first launched in **India** in **May 1997**. ***Hence, it is a document related to Good Governance.***
 
• **National Forest Policy, 1988**: This policy was formulated to ensure environmental stability and maintenance of ecological balance, including atmospheric equilibrium, which are vital for the sustenance of all life forms. Its primary aim was to protect, conserve, and develop forests. It recommended that **33%** of the total land area of the **country** should be under forest or tree cover. ***Hence, this is an environmental policy and NOT a primary document for administrative Good Governance.***
 
• **Second Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC)**: This commission was constituted on **31st August 2005**, under the chairmanship of **Veerappa Moily**, to suggest measures to achieve a proactive, responsive, accountable, sustainable, and efficient administration for the country at all levels of the **Government**. Its **12th Report**, titled **"Citizen Centric Administration: The Heart of Governance,"** is a foundational text for Good Governance. ***Hence, it is a document related to Good Governance.***
 
• **Sevottam Model**: The **Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)** developed the Sevottam model in **2006**. The word **"Sevottam"** is a combination of two Hindi words: **Seva** (Service) and **Uttam** (Excellent). It is a quality management framework applicable to public service delivery organizations to improve the quality of service to citizens. ***Hence, it is a document/model related to Good Governance.***

questions.question: The power of High Courts to issue writs for purposes beyond Fundamental Rights is given under __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 226**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 226** of the **Constitution of India** empowers the **High Courts** to issue directions, orders, or writs, including writs in the nature of **Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**, **Prohibition**, **Quo Warranto**, and **Certiorari**.
 
• The jurisdiction of the **High Court** under **Article 226** is broader than that of the **Supreme Court** under **Article 32** because it can be invoked not only for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** but also for **"any other purpose."**
 
• The phrase **"any other purpose"** refers to the enforcement of an ordinary **legal right** that is not necessarily a fundamental right. *Hence, statement A is correct.*
 
• This power allows the **High Court** to exercise control over administrative actions and ensures that **government authorities** act within the bounds of the law.
 
• The **High Court** can issue these writs to any **person**, **authority**, or **government** located within its **territorial jurisdiction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies):**

 
 
• This article allows citizens to move the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** (Part III of the Constitution).
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** famously described **Article 32** as the **"Heart and Soul of the Constitution."**
 
• Unlike **Article 226**, the **Supreme Court’s** power under this article is limited only to **Fundamental Rights** and cannot be used for ordinary legal rights. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Article 227 (Power of Superintendence):**
 
 
• Every **High Court** has the power of **superintendence** over all **courts and tribunals** throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction.
 
• This includes both **administrative** and **judicial** superintendence, ensuring that subordinate courts function according to the law. *Hence, statement C is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Article 245 (Extent of Legislative Powers):**
 
 
• This article deals with the territorial extent of laws made by **Parliament** and by the **Legislatures of States**.
 
• It specifies that **Parliament** may make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of **India**, and the **State Legislature** for the whole or any part of the **State**. *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Writ Jurisdictions:**

 
 
• While the **Supreme Court's** writ jurisdiction extends to the **entire country**, the **High Court's** jurisdiction is limited to its **state** or **union territory**.
 
• However, the **subject matter** jurisdiction of the **High Court** is wider (Fundamental Rights + Legal Rights) compared to the **Supreme Court** (Fundamental Rights only).
 
 
 
• **Nature of the Power:**
 
 
• The remedy under **Article 32** is itself a **Fundamental Right**, meaning the **Supreme Court** cannot refuse to exercise its power.
 
• In contrast, the remedy under **Article 226** is **discretionary**, meaning the **High Court** may refuse to grant relief if an **alternative remedy** exists.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• The power of **judicial review** under **Article 226** and **Article 32** is considered a **basic feature** of the **Constitution** as per the **L. Chandra Kumar case (1997)**, and it cannot be excluded even by a constitutional amendment.

questions.question: Warli painting, a traditional tribal art form, originates from which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Warli painting** is a traditional tribal art form that originates from the state of **Maharashtra**, specifically practiced by the **Warli tribe** residing in the **North Sahyadri Range**.
 
• The art form is considered one of the oldest in **India**, with roots dating back as far as the **10th century AD**, though its popularity grew significantly in the modern era.
 
• It is characterized by the use of rudimentary geometric shapes: the **circle** (representing the sun and the moon), the **triangle** (derived from mountains and pointed trees), and the **square** (indicating a sacred enclosure or a piece of land).
 
• The central theme of these paintings is the depiction of **social life**, **nature**, and **rituals** rather than mythological characters or deities, which distinguishes it from many other folk arts in **India**.
 
• The **Tarpa dance** is a frequent subject, where the community is shown dancing in circles around a musician playing a **Tarpa** instrument, symbolizing the circle of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Materials and Colors**: The paintings are traditionally done on a **red ochre** (earthy) background made of mud and cow dung. The only color used for the figures is **white**, which is a mixture of **rice paste** and **water** with **gum** as a binding agent.
 
• **Technique**: The artists do not use modern brushes; instead, they use a **bamboo stick** chewed at the end to give it the texture of a paintbrush.
 
• **The Chauk**: A significant element in **Warli art** is the **Chauk** or **Chaukat**, a square frame usually drawn for weddings. Inside the **Chauk**, the goddess **Palaghata** (the goddess of fertility) is depicted.
 
• **Geographic Location**: While primarily centered in the **Palghar**, **Thane**, and **Nashik** districts of **Maharashtra**, the **Warli tribe** and their art are also found in small pockets of **Gujarat** and the Union Territory of **Dadra and Nagar Haveli**.
 
• **Global Recognition**: The art form gained international fame through the efforts of **Jivya Soma Mashe**, who began practicing it as a daily pursuit in the **1970s**, leading to his recognition with the **Padma Shri** award in **2011**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Protection**: **Warli Art** has been registered under the **Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999**, ensuring that the intellectual property rights of the **Warli tribe** in **Maharashtra** are protected.
 
• **Social Context**: Traditionally, **Warli paintings** were created by **women** (known as **Savasini**) to decorate the walls of their huts during **harvests** and **weddings**.
 
• **Style Similarity**: The simplistic and linear style of **Warli** is often compared to the prehistoric rock shelter paintings found at **Bhimbetka** in **Madhya Pradesh**, highlighting its ancient aesthetic appeal.
 
• **Modern Adaptation**: In the **21st century**, **Warli motifs** have moved beyond mud walls to **fabrics**, **stationary**, **home decor**, and **murals** in urban spaces like the **Mumbai** metro and public buildings.

questions.question: Find the number of possible values for a natural number N such that the LCM of 120 and N is 360, and the HCF of 900 and N is 90.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

LCM(120, N) = 360

HCF(900, N) = 90

**Formula Used:**

LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b

Prime factorization method for LCM and HCF

**Calculation:**

⇒ 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5

⇒ 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5

⇒ 900 = 2² × 3² × 5²

⇒ 90 = 2 × 3² × 5

⇒ For LCM(120, N) = 360

⇒ Power of 2 in N ≤ 3

⇒ Power of 3 in N = 2

⇒ Power of 5 in N ≤ 1

⇒ For HCF(900, N) = 90

⇒ Power of 2 in N = 1

⇒ Power of 3 in N ≥ 2

⇒ Power of 5 in N ≥ 1

⇒ Combine conditions:

⇒ Power of 2 = 1

⇒ Power of 3 = 2

⇒ Power of 5 = 1

⇒ N = 2 × 3² × 5

⇒ N = 90

questions.question: The standard deviation of 7 consecutive integers with mean 0 is _______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

7 consecutive integers with mean 0 ⇒ −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3

Use symmetry: variance = (1² + 2² + 3²)×2 / 7

= (1 + 4 + 9)×2 / 7 = 28/7 = 4

SD = √4 = 2

**∴ Answer = 2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

7 consecutive integers with mean 0

**Formula used:**

Standard deviation = √[Σ(x − mean)² / n]

**Calculation:**

⇒ Numbers: −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3

⇒ Mean = 0

⇒ Squares: 9, 4, 1, 0, 1, 4, 9

⇒ Sum = 28

⇒ Variance = 28 / 7 = 4

⇒ Standard deviation = √4 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

Symmetric Data

Variance = average of squared deviations

Standard Deviation

SD = √(variance)
